item.title: NC State vs. Stanford injury report: Duke Scott among many players out
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 20: Luke Mergott #34 of the Duke Blue Devils attempts to tackle Jayden Scott #4 of the North Carolina State Wolfpack during the first half of the game at Wallace Wade Stadium on September 20, 2025 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

item.title: Matt LaFleur Has Strong Take About Jordan Love After Packers’ Win vs. Cowboys
item.description: Matt LaFleur had a strong endorsement for Jordan Love after the Green Bay Packers secured a 23-13 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. The head coach’s emphatic assessment reflected his confidence in the quarterback, who helped guide Green Bay to another important win. LaFleur used a brief but memorable description to express his admiration for Love’s performance. The coach’s praise highlighted the quarterback’s toughness and competitive mindset, qualities that have become increasingly important as the Packers continue building momentum. Green Bay’s latest victory also extended its winning streak to three games, strengthening the team’s position as the season progresses. Sep 7, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) during the game against the Detroit Lions at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Love’s performance against Dallas came as the Packers relied on a balanced effort to control the game. Although the offense did not need to carry the entire burden, the quarterback remained central to Green Bay’s ability to manage possessions and capitalize on opportunities. His presence under center continues to give the team confidence in its ability to compete against quality opposition. Green Bay’s defense also played a significant role in the victory, limiting the Cowboys to 13 points and helping prevent Dallas from generating enough offense to threaten the outcome. The unit’s performance complemented the offense and demonstrated how the Packers can succeed without relying exclusively on explosive passing plays. That balance could prove valuable as the team faces tougher challenges later in the campaign. Matt LaFleur Reacts to Jordan Love’s Performance After Green Bay Packers’ Win Against Dallas Cowboys Dec 7, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Head coach Matt LaFleur looks on during the third quarter against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images LaFleur shared his thoughts about how Love played against the Cowboys in Week 6. This can be seen in a video shared by the league’s official Instagram account. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NFL (@nfl) “He’s a G,” Matt LaFleur said. “We talk about playing like a G. He’s a G.” LaFleur’s comments also underscored the relationship between the coaching staff and its quarterback. item.title: Newcastle Red Bulls sign Canada lock Flesch
item.description: Mason Flesch in action for Canada against the USA in the Pacific Nations Cup in September [Getty Images] Newcastle Red Bulls have signed Canada forward Mason Flesch until the end of the season. The 26-year-old - who can play at lock or in the back row - has been capped 26 times by his country. Flesch scored 10 tries in 11 games for Chicago Hounds, including one in the final as his side overcame California Legion to claim the Major League Rugby title and was named the league's forward of the season for 2026. Ontario-born Flesch came through the ranks with the Toronto Arrows and made his professional debut in 2021 before winning his first Canada cap later that year. Head coach Dan McFarland told the Newcastle website: "Mason has been a stand-out performer in Major League Rugby and for his country, and deserves this opportunity. "He is a great athlete who will add depth to a very competitive area of our squad, and I look forward to working with him in our environment." Flesch, who arrived on Tyneside this week, added: "I'm incredibly excited to be a part of this team. "I'm looking forward to being involved with a quality full-time organisation, and most importantly very eager to train and help push standards." Newcastle have lost their first three Prem games this season and also lost their European Challenge Cup opener 47-14 at Scarlets last Saturday.

item.title: Kansas City Chiefs Announce History After Week 6
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs celebrated a historic defensive achievement by Nick Bolton following their Week 6 victory, adding another milestone to the linebacker’s impressive career. His latest accomplishment highlights his consistency and importance to a defense that continues to play a central role in the team’s pursuit of success. Bolton reached a significant franchise benchmark during Kansas City’s win over the Los Angeles Chargers , reinforcing his reputation as one of the unit’s most dependable players. The achievement reflects his ability to remain productive across multiple seasons while handling the responsibilities that come with being a key figure in the middle of the defense. His impact extends beyond individual statistics, particularly when the Chiefs need leadership and discipline in critical situations. Feb 9, 2025; New Orleans, LA, USA; Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton (32) against the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl LIX at Ceasars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The linebacker has established himself through his tackling, awareness and ability to diagnose plays before opponents can capitalize. His instincts allow him to react quickly against both the run and the pass, while his physical approach helps Kansas City maintain its defensive intensity. Those qualities have made him a valuable part of the team’s structure and helped him build a reputation for reliability. The Week 6 victory also demonstrated how important defensive execution can be when the Chiefs face challenging opponents. Limiting scoring opportunities, making timely stops and forcing offenses into difficult situations can change the course of a game. Bolton’s achievement provides another reminder that Kansas City’s success is not solely dependent on its offensive stars, as defensive contributors continue to establish their own place in franchise history. Kansas City Chiefs Flex Nick Bolton Achievement After Week 6 Jan 26, 2025; Kansas City, MO, USA; Linebacker Nick Bolton (32) celebrates after defeating the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Championship game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Bolton’s franchise achievement has turned a lot of heads toward his direction. This can be seen in a post shared by the team’s official Instagram account. item.title: Jack Munro Keeps On Winning At The Association Of Pickleball Players 2026 Louisville Open
item.description: Jack Munro (L) and Richard Livornese (R) win their 7th straight Men's Doubles pro title on the APP. APP The Association of Pickleball Players (APP) held its eighth domestic full points event of the 2026 season this past weekend, and became the first pro tour to ever play an event in Kentucky, with the 2026 Humana APP Louisville Open. The tour played this event at the Kentucky International Convention Center in downtown Louisville, and its players got to visit all the attractions that Louisville is known for. Click here for the PickleballDen.com home page for the event , where you can get tournament details, draw sheets, and results. News and Noteworthy ahead of the Event Here’s a quick recap of notable news items of import to the tour or this event: 10/8/26: APP announces its fy2027 slate of domestic events , featuring 12 events (one a month) around the country. new sites for 2027 include Palm Beach Gardens, and an Arizona spot in December; the rest are returning core events from the 2026 slate. 9/22/26: The APP announces the APP Moneyball Series . APP Moneyball Series is a new competitive series for current and aspiring professional pickleball players, offering high-level local competition, prize money, APP Tour ranking points, and a pathway to national and global events. With that said, let’s recap the action. Men’s Pro Singles Recap Men’s Singles on the APP continues to show parity, with 6 distinct winners in the last 9 events held. The winner from the last event (Tristan Dussault) was upset in the round of 16 by Jake Bower, and five of the eight top seeds in the draw failed to advance to the quarters. However, the final ended up being 1v2, with the tour’s top ranked player Ronan Camron taking out No. 2 Dusty Boyer for his 3rd career singles title. Veteran Eduardo Irizarry pipped Bower for the Bronze. Gold : Ronan Camron. Silver : Dusty Boyer. Bronze : Eduardo Irizarry. Women’s Pro Singles Recap After several events of chaos in the Women’s singles draw, this one went almost completely chalk from beginning to end. The only interloper double-digit seed into the quarters was Australian Roos van Reek (who’s talents are not matched by her seed), who fell at that juncture to fellow No. 4 seed Aussie Seone Mendez. From there, the top players on tour battled it out in the semis and finals to great effect. Turkovic got her second APP singles title in a row with a 3-game upset win over Stewart to close the gap at the top of the rankings. Gold : Domenika Turkovic. Silver : Kat Stewart. Bronze : Bobbi Oshiro. item.content:encoded: Jack Munro (L) and Richard Livornese (R) win their 7th straight Men's Doubles pro title on the APP. APP The Association of Pickleball Players (APP) held its eighth domestic full points event of the 2026 season this past weekend, and became the first pro tour to ever play an event in Kentucky, with the 2026 Humana APP Louisville Open. The tour played this event at the Kentucky International Convention Center in downtown Louisville, and its players got to visit all the attractions that Louisville is known for. Click here for the PickleballDen.com home page for the event , where you can get tournament details, draw sheets, and results. News and Noteworthy ahead of the Event Here’s a quick recap of notable news items of import to the tour or this event: 10/8/26: APP announces its fy2027 slate of domestic events , featuring 12 events (one a month) around the country. new sites for 2027 include Palm Beach Gardens, and an Arizona spot in December; the rest are returning core events from the 2026 slate. 9/22/26: The APP announces the APP Moneyball Series . APP Moneyball Series is a new competitive series for current and aspiring professional pickleball players, offering high-level local competition, prize money, APP Tour ranking points, and a pathway to national and global events. With that said, let’s recap the action. Men’s Pro Singles Recap Men’s Singles on the APP continues to show parity, with 6 distinct winners in the last 9 events held. The winner from the last event (Tristan Dussault) was upset in the round of 16 by Jake Bower, and five of the eight top seeds in the draw failed to advance to the quarters. However, the final ended up being 1v2, with the tour’s top ranked player Ronan Camron taking out No. 2 Dusty Boyer for his 3rd career singles title. Veteran Eduardo Irizarry pipped Bower for the Bronze. Gold : Ronan Camron. Silver : Dusty Boyer. Bronze : Eduardo Irizarry. Women’s Pro Singles Recap After several events of chaos in the Women’s singles draw, this one went almost completely chalk from beginning to end. The only interloper double-digit seed into the quarters was Australian Roos van Reek (who’s talents are not matched by her seed), who fell at that juncture to fellow No. 4 seed Aussie Seone Mendez. From there, the top players on tour battled it out in the semis and finals to great effect. No. 1 Stewart went three games and edged Mendez 11-9 in one semi, while No. 2 Domenika Turkovic also had to dig deep to top No. 3 Oshiro. In the final. Turkovic got her second APP singles title in a row with a 3-game upset win over Stewart to close the gap at the top of the rankings. Gold : Domenika Turkovic. Silver : Kat Stewart. Bronze : Bobbi Oshiro. Mixed Pro Doubles Recap One of the “fun” things that happen when a player of the quality of Jay Devilliers suddenly parachutes into a tour is the propensity for very low seeds to make very big runs. In mixed, Devilliers paired with Domenika Turkovic to create a very formidable, but very under-seeded Mixed team. They met the top seeds in the round of 16 in No. 1 Megan Fudge & Aiden Schenk, and moved past them with relative ease 6,4. In fact, Devilliers & Turkovic made it all the way to the final, with multiple additional upsets along the way. In the final, they ran into the tour’s top ranked Mixed Male player in Jack Munro, playing this week with the visiting Australian Roos van Reek, and they made the most of the trip, beating Jay & Domenika for gold. Gold : van Reek & Munro. Silver : turkovic & Devilliers. Bronze : Stewart & Livornese. Men’s Pro Doubles Recap The Men’s doubles draw was shaken early, when the No. 2 seeds Palm & Camron were ousted in the first round by Shay Hugo & Kevin Caulfield. This opened up an opportunity on the bottom half for the veteran No. 15 seeds Naveen Beasley & Max Wild, and they made a run to the semis before falling. However, it was all for naught, as the top seeds Jack Munro & Richard Livornese Jr. were not to be denied. The No. 1 seeds won their 7th straight APP Men’s Doubles draw, beating No. 3 Aidan Schenk & Zack Marceau in the final. Jay Devilliers & Tanner Tomassi, silver medalists in Columbus two weeks ago, salvaged the bronze. Gold : Munro & Livornese. Silver : Schenk & Marceau. Bronze : Devilliers & Tomassi. Women’s Pro Doubles Recap Kat Stewart (L) and Bobbi Oshiro (R) cruised to the Women's Doubles title. APP On the backs of two gold medals in the last few events, Shelby Bates & Christine Maddox have taken over the No. 1 team spot on tour, but they ran into the buzz saw that is Glauka Carvajal Lane lately. She’s taken three straight APP/APP International silver medals lately, with three different partners. In Kentucky, Lane paired up with Domenika Turkovic, with whom she won silver in Columbus two weeks ago, and they took out the top seeds in the semi to push for another gold. In the final, they met No. 3 Bobbi Oshiro & Kat Stewart, who took out the under-seeded No. 10 pair of Vivian Glozman & Roos van Reek in dominant fashion in the bottom semi. In the final, it was another bridesmaid day for Lane and Turkovic, losing 2,9 for another silver medal. Kat Stewart finishes the event with 3 medals: a Gold, a Silver, and a Bronze. Gold : Oshiro & Stewart. Silver : Lane & Turkovic. Bronze : Bates & Maddox. AARP Champions Pro Competition Quick Recap Men’s Champions Pro Singles: APP No. 1 Youssef Bouzidi crushed No. 2 Marcello Jardim for the title, the 9th time in the last 10 Champions pro singles draws these two met for gold. Women’s Champions Pro Singles: With the APP No. 1 Karin Ptaszek-Kochis missing, newcomer and shoe-in for Rookie of the Year Carolina Lopez Ascarate dominated Lee Whitwell for gold. Men’s Champions Pro Doubles: Youssef Bouzidi made it a double, teaming with Dayne Gingrich to win the Doubles title as the top seeds. Women’s Champions Pro Doubles: The two singles finalists, Ascarate & Whitwell, teamed up to cruise to the Doubles title together. Mixed Champions Pro Doubles: Carolina Lopez Ascarate/Marcello Jardim took the mixed title as the No. 2 seeds, securing the triple crown for Carolina Lopez Ascarate for the weekend, her first. AARP Masters 60+ Pro Competition Quick Recap Men’s Masters 60+ Pro Singles: Adam Painter took the Singles 60+ as the No. 3 seed. Men’s Masters 60+ Pro Doubles: APP 60+ newcomers Rich Lively & Ross Weinberg shocked the field and took the title. Shoutout to Weinberg, a Virginia native and an old racquetball colleague of mine from years ago here in the state. Women’s Masters 60+ Pro Doubles: Ginny Purdy & Heather Iffert ( did double duty also playing Champions pro this weekend) took the 60+ Women’s doubles title. Mixed Masters 60+ Pro Doubles: Heather Iffert got the 60+ pro double by winning Mixed with Mark Wilder. The Pro Pickleball Medal Tracker spreadsheets have now been updated with these results. Click here for the Pro-only Medal Tracker , and click here for the Senior Pro Medal Tracker . These spreadsheets hold Medal winners for every pro event going back to the beginnings of the tours. Next up on the Pickleball Calendar? According to my Master Pickleball Schedule , Next up for the APP is the 2026 Dubai Open this coming weekend. They also have Next and Collegiate events over the next couple of weeks, and then more international events planned in Mid November. Their next domestic tournament is 11/15 weekend in Arizona. item.title: Christopher Nkunku ‘can imagine’ staying at RB Leipzig
item.description: Christopher Nkunku ‘can imagine’ staying at RB Leipzig Christopher Nkunku (28) has struck four goals and provided two assists in eight appearances across all competitions since returning to RB Leipzig on loan from Serie A outfit Milan. Gearing up ahead of Wednesday’s UEFA Champions League clash against Real Madrid, the Frenchman stated that he could imagine staying at the Saxony club beyond his current loan, which expires in June 2027. “I’m very happy,” Nkunku told Sport Bild . “I feel very comfortable in the city and at the club. Of course, I can very well imagine staying longer.” During his first spell at Leipzig between 2019 and 2023, the Frenchman registered 47 goals and 43 assists in 119 Bundesliga appearances before departing for Chelsea. “I had some very significant moments in my career and my life in Leipzig and with RB,” he explained. “I really enjoyed those four years. But, above all, the clubs would have to reach an agreement at the end of the season, so it’s not just up to me.” GGFN | Daniel Pinder

item.title: ‘You shouldn’t be able to represent the USA’: Riley Gaines not happy as WNBA players skip national anthem
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have drawn plenty of criticism from conservative corners of the internet after both teams left the court before the national anthem during the first two games of the WNBA Finals. Now, one of the WNBA’s most vocal critics has weighed in. Anti-trans activist and former Kentucky swimmer Riley Gaines suggested that players who kneel for the anthem should be barred from playing for Team USA at the Olympics. It’s a very aggressive argument from Gaines, but there’s just one problem: nobody actually knelt during the national anthem. Teams Leave Court for Anthem Before Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday, both teams were warming up at Chase Center before they left the court shortly before the anthem . They then jogged back onto the floor just seconds after it ended. The same thing happened again before Game 2 on Monday night, according to Fox News . Neither the teams nor the league has explained why the players left the court. OutKick has pointed to the WNBA’s rulebook, which calls for players, coaches, and trainers to stand in a line during the anthem. But that rule only appears to apply if the players are on the court, and it doesn’t seem to require them to be there in the first place. It’s also not clear whether the moment was intentional. Leaving the floor at a set time before tipoff isn’t uncommon in basketball, and LSU head coach Kim Mulkey gave a similar explanation in 2024 when her team, which included current Dream star Angel Reese, was off the court for the anthem before an Elite Eight game against Iowa. ‘You shouldn’t be able to represent the USA’ Gaines shared her take on X on Tuesday while quote-posting a clip of the teams leaving the court before Game 2. “It’s my personal opinion that if you kneel for the flag and what it represents, you shouldn’t be able to represent the USA at the Olympics,” Gaines wrote . The post went viral, racking up tens of thousands of likes. But it’s worth noting that Gaines’ criticism wasn’t necessarily based on reality, as the players did not actually kneel during the national anthem, they just weren’t on the floor at all. Gaines has become one of the WNBA’s most prominent critics in recent months, particularly when it comes to transgender athletes in women’s sports . Ever since tying transgender swimmer Lia Thomas for fifth at the 2022 NCAA Championships, Gaines has built a platform speaking out against transgender women competing in women’s sports. She now hosts The Riley Gaines Show for OutKick, which was rebranded from Gaines for Girls in January to cover broader political commentary. This month, she has also been touring college campuses with Turning Point USA . The post ‘You shouldn’t be able to represent the USA’: Riley Gaines not happy as WNBA players skip national anthem appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Indicates Trade Stance After Concerning Development
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers keep on winning . In fact, they have not tasted defeat so far in the 2026 NFL season, as they improved to 6-0 after thwarting Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders in Week 6’s 23-17 win at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara on Monday. But the Niners are not without problems. For one, they have an unenviable situation in their wide receiver room, with plenty of hurt bodies in the group. Star wide receiver Mike Evans just aggravated an Achilles issue in the Commanders game, and it forced him to leave the contest in the first half. He was unable to return to the game, though, he still ended up leading all San Francisco players with 94 receiving yards on three receptions and five targets. Will The 49ers Address Their Wide Receiver Situation With a Big Trade? Sep 11, 2026; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) at press conference after the 2026 NFL Melbourne Game against the Los Angeles Rams at Melbourne Cricket Ground. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Apart from Evans, the Niners also have Ricky Pearsall, De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Christian Kirk, all with injury designations. All those players sat out the game against the Commanders. Some of them could potentially return sooner rather than later, but as it stands, San Francisco’s wide receiver unit is far from its best shape. A trade could help ease the problem in the group for San Francisco, but an acquisition via that route doesn’t seem likely at the moment. Via Nick Wagoner of ESPN : All of that attrition would seem to set the stage for a trade, though Shanahan indicated the team might stick with what it has for another week and then see where things stand after the bye. Nevertheless, San Francisco’s offense has been among the most prolific in the league, putting up 29.5 points and 366.7 total yards per game, both top 10 in the league to date. Coming up next for the Niners is a Week 7 game against the Atlanta Falcons on the road. Sep 14, 2025; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan looks at the score board as he leaves the field at the end of game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome. item.title: Post-Wuhan WTA Power Rankings: Rybakina Leads, But Who Is Her Biggest Threat?
item.description: Tennis - U.S. Open - Flushing Meadows, New York, United States - September 12, 2026 Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina celebrates with the winner's trophy after her final match against Belarus' Aryna Sabalenka IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Robert Deutsch | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith The WTA season is nearing its conclusion, and the landscape looks quite different from what we saw in our pre-Wimbledon WTA power rankings . Elena Rybakina has established herself as the dominant player of 2026, Linda Noskova has become a Grand Slam champion, Mirra Andreeva continues to make extraordinary progress, and Aryna Sabalenka has experienced an unexpected decline. Meanwhile, Maja Chwalinska has emerged as one of the season’s most remarkable stories, following her Roland Garros final with an unlikely Wuhan Masters title. As always, these are not simply the WTA rankings. They combine season-long accomplishments, recent form, consistency, performances against elite opposition, and the level each player can produce heading into the final stretch. Players currently sidelined by injury, including Amanda Anisimova, are excluded. With the WTA Finals approaching, here is the updated order. Post-Wuhan WTA Power Rankings 1. Elena Rybakina WTA Ranking: No. 1 Previous Power Ranking: 2 There is no serious argument against Rybakina occupying the top position in the WTA power rankings. The Kazakhstani has won the Australian Open and US Open, defeating Sabalenka in both finals, and earned 7,503 Race points. Her 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory over Sabalenka in New York was particularly impressive, securing her third Grand Slam title and ultimately the world No. 1 ranking. Rybakina’s serve remains arguably the most effective weapon in women’s tennis, while her flat, powerful groundstrokes allow her to dictate rallies without relying on spectacular defensive movement. However, her recent physical problems cannot be ignored. A recurring foot and lower-leg issue contributed to her Cincinnati retirement and subsequent withdrawal from Wuhan. She also suffered a surprising opening-round defeat to Alina Charaeva in Beijing. She is scheduled to return in Ningbo, but her fitness remains the biggest question heading into the WTA Finals. If healthy, she is the obvious favourite. 2. Mirra Andreeva WTA Ranking: No. 3 Previous Power Ranking: 3 Andreeva’s first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros was already enough to establish 2026 as the most important season of her career. But the 19-year-old has continued improving. Her run to the Beijing final demonstrated that her success in Paris was hardly a one-off, even if Qinwen Zheng eventually defeated her 7-5 6-4. Andreeva now sits third in the Race with more than 6,300 points. Her greatest strength remains her remarkable tactical understanding. She can absorb pace, redirect shots and disrupt opponents without taking unnecessary risks. However, her US Open quarter-final defeat to Coco Gauff exposed an area that still needs improvement. item.content:encoded: Tennis - U.S. Open - Flushing Meadows, New York, United States - September 12, 2026 Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina celebrates with the winner's trophy after her final match against Belarus' Aryna Sabalenka IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Robert Deutsch | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith The WTA season is nearing its conclusion, and the landscape looks quite different from what we saw in our pre-Wimbledon WTA power rankings . Elena Rybakina has established herself as the dominant player of 2026, Linda Noskova has become a Grand Slam champion, Mirra Andreeva continues to make extraordinary progress, and Aryna Sabalenka has experienced an unexpected decline. Meanwhile, Maja Chwalinska has emerged as one of the season’s most remarkable stories, following her Roland Garros final with an unlikely Wuhan Masters title. As always, these are not simply the WTA rankings. They combine season-long accomplishments, recent form, consistency, performances against elite opposition, and the level each player can produce heading into the final stretch. Players currently sidelined by injury, including Amanda Anisimova, are excluded. With the WTA Finals approaching, here is the updated order. Post-Wuhan WTA Power Rankings 1. Elena Rybakina WTA Ranking: No. 1 Previous Power Ranking: 2 There is no serious argument against Rybakina occupying the top position in the WTA power rankings. The Kazakhstani has won the Australian Open and US Open, defeating Sabalenka in both finals, and earned 7,503 Race points. Her 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory over Sabalenka in New York was particularly impressive, securing her third Grand Slam title and ultimately the world No. 1 ranking. Rybakina’s serve remains arguably the most effective weapon in women’s tennis, while her flat, powerful groundstrokes allow her to dictate rallies without relying on spectacular defensive movement. However, her recent physical problems cannot be ignored. A recurring foot and lower-leg issue contributed to her Cincinnati retirement and subsequent withdrawal from Wuhan. She also suffered a surprising opening-round defeat to Alina Charaeva in Beijing. She is scheduled to return in Ningbo, but her fitness remains the biggest question heading into the WTA Finals. If healthy, she is the obvious favourite. 2. Mirra Andreeva WTA Ranking: No. 3 Previous Power Ranking: 3 Andreeva’s first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros was already enough to establish 2026 as the most important season of her career. But the 19-year-old has continued improving. Her run to the Beijing final demonstrated that her success in Paris was hardly a one-off, even if Qinwen Zheng eventually defeated her 7-5 6-4. Andreeva now sits third in the Race with more than 6,300 points. Her greatest strength remains her remarkable tactical understanding. She can absorb pace, redirect shots and disrupt opponents without taking unnecessary risks. However, her US Open quarter-final defeat to Coco Gauff exposed an area that still needs improvement. Andreeva led 6-2 and held two match points in the second-set tiebreak before losing in three sets. Those setbacks are part of her development, but they also prevent her from challenging Rybakina for the top position. Still, she might be the most complete young player on Tour. 3. Linda Noskova WTA Ranking: No. 8 Previous Power Ranking: 9 Noskova arrived at Wimbledon after winning the Berlin title, but few would have predicted she would leave London as a Grand Slam champion. The Czech defeated Karolina Muchova 6-2 5-7 6-3 in the final, completing an extraordinary grass-court season. She then reached the US Open quarter-finals, pushing Sabalenka to three sets before narrowly losing. Noskova’s powerful serve and aggressive groundstrokes make her particularly dangerous when conditions reward first-strike tennis. Unlike some players with similar weapons, however, she has become increasingly comfortable constructing points rather than simply attempting to hit through opponents. Her game still has inconsistencies, and her recent Asian swing has not been especially impressive. Nevertheless, winning Wimbledon and Berlin in the same season deserves enormous recognition. At 21, Noskova has already accomplished something most players never will, earning her spot at No. 3 in the WTA power rankings. 4. Aryna Sabalenka WTA Ranking: No. 2 Previous Power Ranking: 1 Sabalenka’s decline is one of the season’s more surprising developments. She began 2026 by winning 26 of her first 27 matches, completing the Sunshine Double and looking almost unbeatable. Since Miami, however, her results have deteriorated considerably. The Belarusian has not won another title and has lost two Grand Slam finals against Rybakina. Her latest defeat against Ann Li in Wuhan was really worrying. Sabalenka led 6-3 4-2 before losing 3-6 6-4 7-6, committing 44 unforced errors in another match that slipped away from a winning position. The problem is not a lack of weapons; it never was. Her serve, return and aggressive groundstrokes remain among the best on Tour. But her error management has deteriorated, and she has repeatedly struggled to maintain control after establishing an advantage. Sabalenka’s ceiling remains extraordinarily high. Right now, however, her consistency does not justify a higher position in the WTA power rankings. 5. Coco Gauff WTA Ranking: No. 5 Previous Power Ranking: 8 Gauff has enjoyed an encouraging second half of the season. Her Cincinnati title was very impressive, culminating in a victory over Jessica Pegula in the final. She followed that success by reaching the US Open semi-finals, where her remarkable comeback against Andreeva demonstrated why she remains one of the toughest competitors in women’s tennis. Her defensive movement remains exceptional, while improvements to her serve have made her considerably more competitive on hard courts. However, she still has occasional problems with her forehand, especially when opponents consistently attack that side. Those vulnerabilities prevent her from producing the same relentless baseline pressure as Rybakina or Sabalenka at their best. Still, she has qualified for another WTA Finals and deserves consideration as a serious contender. 6. Jessica Pegula WTA Ranking: No. 4 Previous Power Ranking: 5 Pegula remains one of the most reliable performers on the WTA Tour. She has won titles in Dubai and Charleston, reached the Cincinnati final, and qualified for another WTA Finals appearance. Her consistency is impressive. She rarely relies on overwhelming power. Instead, she takes the ball early, redirects pace and uses excellent court positioning to pressure opponents. Her ability to maintain a high baseline level makes her extremely difficult to beat. However, the same question still follows her. Can she produce enough exceptional tennis to defeat the very best players across several consecutive matches? Her Cincinnati defeat to Gauff was disappointing, while a second-round loss to Jelena Ostapenko in Wuhan did little to improve her recent form. Pegula remains a credible threat, but she is not currently playing quite well enough to challenge the leading contenders in the WTA power rankings. 7. Maja Chwalinska WTA Ranking: No. 11 Previous Power Ranking: NR Perhaps the most remarkable story in women’s tennis this season . Chwalinska entered Roland Garros as a qualifier and somehow reached the final, eventually losing to Andreeva. That achievement alone would have been extraordinary. But the Polish player has now added a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan. Her run included a 7-5 6-1 semi-final victory over Iga Swiatek before she recovered from a set down to defeat Sonay Kartal 2-6 6-4 6-2 in the final. Chwalinska does not have the overwhelming power of some players. Her game relies on intelligent shot placement, variation, and the ability to disrupt opponents’ preferred patterns. She uses angles exceptionally well and is comfortable changing the ball’s direction and height. The

item.title: Here’s how the Browns have a Chance for not only a Winning Record, but a Playoff Spot
item.description: theOBR BEREA, Ohio — Former NFL coach Jim Mora famously was asked after a loss if his Colts team could still make the playoffs. His answer became a famous meme. “’Playoffs? Don’t talk about—playoffs? You kidding me? Playoffs?! I just hope we can win a game! Another game!” Don’t look now, but the Browns are 4-2 (2-0 AFC North). Despite not playing well on offense on a regular, consistent basis, the offense has been able to score when needed, to get wins in four, fourth quarter games. No matter how they got to 4-2, their record is what it is and it has put them in position to do some things that were not imagined by most before the season started. The Browns have not been in first place in the division this late in the season, since the 2014 season, when they were 6-3 after nine games. Unfortunately that season, the Browns went 1-6 the rest of the way that season, finished 7-9 and missed the playoffs. Currently, the Browns would make the playoffs as the division winner, due to tiebreakers. They would be the No. 4 seed in the playoffs and host a first-round game. The only two teams in the AFC with better records than the Browns are the Chiefs (5-0) and the Bills (5-1). The Jaguars lead their division at 4-2, while the Patriots, Broncos, Steelers and Ravens are all 4-2. We thought the Browns would win between five and nine games, if everything went right for them. We picked them to be 6-11. To get to nine wins, they had to have average to above average quarterback play—and to this point, they have. With 11 games to play, the Browns could play below .500 the rest of the way and still have a winning record. A 5-6 record in the final 11 games gets the Browns to 9-8. To put that into perspective, the Browns have only had four winning seasons since the team returned in 1999: 2002 (9-7), 2007 (10-6), 2020 (11-5) and 2023 (11-6). They've made the playoffs three times, 2002, 2020 and 2023, all three as a wild card team. The Browns have never won the AFC North. The last time they won their division was in 1989, when it was the AFC Central. When told the betting odds before the season had the Browns winning 5 1/2 games, owner Jimmy Haslam said he would take the ‘over’ during training camp. If the Browns go 6-5 the rest of the way, they would finish 10-7, likely being in the mix for a playoff spot, either as the winner of the AFC North or as a wild card team. We picked them to be 6-11. To get to nine wins, they had to have average to above average quarterback play—and to this point, they have. With 11 games to play, the Browns could play below .500 the rest of the way and still have a winning record. A 5-6 record in the final 11 games gets the Browns to 9-8. To put that into perspective, the Browns have only had four winning seasons since the team returned in 1999: 2002 (9-7), 2007 (10-6), 2020 (11-5) and 2023 (11-6). They've made the playoffs three times, 2002, 2020 and 2023, all three as a wild card team. The Browns have never won the AFC North. The last time they won their division was in 1989, when it was the AFC Central. When told the betting odds before the season had the Browns winning 5 1/2 games, owner Jimmy Haslam said he would take the ‘over’ during training camp. If the Browns go 6-5 the rest of the way, they would finish 10-7, likely being in the mix for a playoff spot, either as the winner of the AFC North or as a wild card team. Currently, six AFC teams are 2-4 or worse, leaving 10 of the remaining 16 teams in the AFC in contention. Seven teams make the playoffs, including four division winners and three wild card teams. According to The Providence Journal , NFL teams that start a season 2-4 manage to make the playoffs, only 9-19 percent of the time. The long-term historical rate (since 1990) found that of the 205 NFL teams that started 2-4, only 9.3 percent of those teams made the playoffs. The recent trend, since playoffs were expanded to seven teams in both conferences in 2020, the success has been higher. About 19 percent of teams that started the season 2-4 made the playoffs. The most recent team to start 2-4 and make the playoffs was the Titans in 2019, who started 2-4 and finished with a 9-7 record. Of the 16 AFC teams, six have records of 2-4 or worse. Although teams have turned it around before after a 2-4 start, the odds are only 9-19 percent of making the playoffs, likely leaving 10 teams fighting for seven playoff spots. With that said, here are the records of the teams the Browns have on their schedule the rest of the way and their current records. @ Titans (1-5) @ Steelers (4-2) @ Saints (2-4) Texans (2-4) Raiders (3-3) Bengals (3-2) Falcons (2-4) @ Giants (3-2-1) @ Ravens (4-2) Colts (2-4) @ Bengals (3-2) Only five of the games are against teams, currently with a winning record. Four of those five games are in the AFC North. The only teams on the schedule with a winning record that is not in the AFC North is the Giants, who are currently 3-2-1. The overall record for the teams the Browns play the rest of the way is 29-34-1 for a winning percentage of .461. According to the website, Tankathon.com , the Browns have the fifth-easiest schedule remaining in the NFL. Eleven games is a long way to go in the NFL and things can go sideways quickly, as Browns fans know so well, but there is hope for the Browns and the journey continues on Sunday against the 1-5 Titans.

item.title: Nvidia picks OpenShell to tame AI gents
item.description: Nvidia has proposed a new way to keep corporate AI agents in line. Nvidia on Wednesday introduced its OpenShell Reference Architecture . Based on the company's OpenShell secure runtime, It's a recipe for creating, operating, observing, and policing AI agents using OpenShell on Nvidia hardware. "Nvidia created OpenShell to give agents the freedom to do useful work within clearly defined boundaries — contained, monitored and under control," CEO Jensen Huang said in a canned statement. "With the OpenShell Reference Architecture, agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera and be governed on BlueField." AI agents are touted as a powerful automation technology. The reality is that they can be unruly, as demonstrated by security testing OpenAI and Anthropic conducted, during which their models exceeded their remit and attacked third-party organizations. Developers of existing agents, like Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and OpenCode, therefore include controls that limit access to tools like curl and bash. Devs also create sandboxes to isolate an agentic process from the host, so that if agents go awry they're contained. OpenShell sits a level above that with a runtime that extends sandboxing to govern gateway-brokered credentials, identity and policy boundaries, and (eventually) routing and workflows too. At least mostly – OpenShell still has a few open security-related issues listed on GitHub. To implement OpenShell, organizations need Nvidia hardware. The company's blueprint calls for Nvidia Vera Rubin infrastructure to run models like Nvidia Nemotron, with agent harnesses handled via Vera CPUs, and Nvidia BlueField-4 DPUs (aka SmartNICs) propping up Nvidia Sentry security software to monitor agent behavior. The AI biz has made this blueprint available to partners capable of powering Linux and Kubernetes infrastructure. The usual suspects are aboard: Canonical, SUSE and Red Hat. Cloud hyperscalers Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure have also been tapped as vendors for this vision. And of course Nvidia's floor plan applies to agents from various model builders, including Anthropic, Cohere, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Perplexity, Reflection, and SpaceX. Nvidia says several banks – Europe’s BBVA and Santander – are perusing the OpenShell Reference Architecture spec to see how it aligns with their security and governance requirements. And the AI biz is not too modest to let slip that SAP is integrating the OpenShell Reference Architecture with its Joule Studio runtime for safer agent operations. It's worth noting that OpenShell collects telemetry data by default, "to improve the project," Nvidia insists. The biz allows users to opt-out, with a cautionary note: "Third-party services, model providers, inference endpoints, agents, or tools that you configure and use with OpenShell may have their own terms and privacy practices." ®

item.title: Nvidia's grand plan for speeding up datacenter deployments: AI trailer parks
item.description: Datacenters are taking too long to bring online to fill the demand of the AI boom. So starting in 2027, Nvidia and its partners will offer its Vera Rubin rack systems fully plumbed, wired, and ready for deployment in modular bit barns. The containers, which Nvidia calls DSX pods, were unveiled at GTC Berlin this week and are essentially the datacenter equivalent of a trailer home. Built by partners like HPE, Dell, Schneider Electric, and others, each DSX pod will come fully furnished with all the compute, interconnects, electrical, and plumbing a growing AI factory might need. Just drop the pod on a prepared datacenter site, hook up power, networking, and cooling, and you'll be churning out tokens and raking in profit in no time. Or that's Nvidia's sales pitch anyway. Inside the 28 metric ton containers you'll find seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks packing 504 GPUs and 252 Vera CPUs. GPUzilla says the pods will cut datacenter deployment times from six months to as little as two weeks because it will validate every fitting, cable, and component before it leaves the factory. The idea being if there is something wrong, it'll get caught there rather than after customers have gone through the trouble of hooking everything up. And just like a trailer home, Nvidia's DSX pods will be entirely customizable. Prefer HPE over Dell, or Eaton over Schneider? No problem, Nvidia has roped all its buddies into building these compute containers. And if you ever need more compute, just add another trailer and you've got yourself a double wide, which will surely be the envy of all your neocloud neighbors. The first DSX pods powered by Nvidia's Vera Rubin rack systems should roll off the production line early next year, and reflect the company's ongoing effort to quash supply chain challenges before they start eating into revenues. Also at GTC Berlin, Nvidia laid out out new DSX specs for waterless datacenters, which use closed loop coolants and dry coolers rather than water-thirsty cooling towers. This effort builds on work announced at the AI Infra Summit earlier this year, when Nvidia touted its effeorts to squeeze more performance out of less juice , while also allowing bit barns to spin down their workloads in response to changing grid conditions. ®

And just like a trailer home, Nvidia's DSX pods will be entirely customizable. Prefer HPE over Dell, or Eaton over Schneider? No problem, Nvidia has roped all its buddies into building these compute containers. And if you ever need more compute, just add another trailer and you've got yourself a double wide, which will surely be the envy of all your neocloud neighbors. The first DSX pods powered by Nvidia's Vera Rubin rack systems should roll off the production line early next year, and reflect the company's ongoing effort to quash supply chain challenges before they start eating into revenues. Also at GTC Berlin, Nvidia laid out out new DSX specs for waterless datacenters, which use closed loop coolants and dry coolers rather than water-thirsty cooling towers. This effort builds on work announced at the AI Infra Summit earlier this year, when Nvidia touted its effeorts to squeeze more performance out of less juice , while also allowing bit barns to spin down their workloads in response to changing grid conditions. ®

item.title: Indiana football’s defense is still championship-level, as shown by the Ohio State game
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - SEPTEMBER 25: Indiana Hoosiers Defensive Coordinator Bryant Haines prior to a college football game between the Northwestern Wildcats and Indiana Hoosiers on September 25, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana’s heavyweight bout with Ohio State this past weekend taught us a few things about this team. One of the most important lessons came from the defense, which looked like a another championship unit despite the loss to the Buckeyes at home. Bryant Haines is the best assistant coach in college football and he has the hardware to prove it as last season’s Broyles Award winner. As long as he’s with the program, the Hoosiers will have a strong defense. He’s done more great work with this group. Indiana had to replace cornerstones like Aiden Fisher, Mikail Kamara, D’Angelo Ponds and Louis Moore, among others, in building out this group. This new unit leans on Isaiah Jones and Rolijah Hardy at linebacker with freshman Jacob Savage showing he can play right away alongside them. Jamari Sharpe slid up as Indiana’s No. 1 cornerback with Penn State transfer AJ Harris taking over at No. 2. Wisconsin transfer Preston Zachman took over at safety while Byron Baldwin slid up at rover. Amare Ferrell stayed put and remains as vital as ever. Indiana’s defensive interior of Tyrique Tucker and Mario Landino remains as good as ever with Tulsa transfer Joe Hjelle and freshman Blake Smythe proving impactful as well. The additions of Tobi Osunsanmi and Chiddi Obiazor along with the late retentions of Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt have proven stout as well. Indiana had a lot to replace. It did so about as well as it could’ve. The secondary took some heat early on this season with some warning signs in non-conference play and against Northwestern but that group, as its predecessors did in 2025, has tightened up and played better in recent weeks, especially as Harris has returned to the lineup. The result of all this was holding Ohio State to its lowest scoring output of the season up to this point. The Hoosiers managed four sacks, six and a half tackles for loss and a pair of interceptions out of the Buckeyes in keeping the game close as the offense worked to figure out its own issues with Ohio State’s defense. Indiana even managed to largely contain Jeremiah Smith’s impact of the game. Between exploiting Julian Sayin’s reliance on Smith to going after the quarterback, the Hoosiers limited the star wide receiver to four receptions and 68 yards. Outside of a lone blown coverage in the endzone (a huge deal! yes! but!), Indiana kept Smith from doing too much damage. If Indiana can do that to Ohio State, it can do so to just about anyone. The Hoosier defense kept that 2025 team in games against Iowa, Oregon, Penn State and Ohio State itself while the offense figured out what it needed to do to win. item.title: Do you know why Harry Kane is poised to make history at the Ballon d’Or?
item.description: (Photo by Reinaldo Coddou H./Bundesliga via Getty Images) | Bundesliga via Getty Images Bayern Munich has known its fair share of legendary strikers. Harry Kane follows in the footsteps of giants, from Gerd Müller to Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, from Giovane Élber and Luca Toni to Robert Lewandowski in the most recent past. Few won the biggest individual prize football has to offer. One was arguably robbed (twice!). In the coming days, Kane stands a chance of cementing himself in history. His record speaks for itself. Seventy-three goals last season means he will be awarded the Müller Trophy, given to the highest scorer from the past season. This will be the England captain’s second time winning the award, with both instances coming after his move to FC Bayern in 2023. In this case, club and player have found a winning combination that elevates each other. So, what accolades await the 33-year-old at the Ballon d’Or ceremony? Well, let’s recap: He will become the second player to win two Müller Trophies, following in the footsteps of Robert Lewandowski, who also did it with Bayern Munich. He could become the first Ballon d’Or winner who also won the Müller Trophy the same year. Both Erling Haaland and Robert Lewandowski had a shot, but they never got the big prize due to extenuating circumstances. He could become the fourth Bayern Munich player to win the Ballon d’Or, after Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge. In the same vein, he would become the seventh player to lift the Ballon d’Or while playing for a Bundesliga club. Following on to that stat, he would become the fifth English player and the seventh British player to win a Ballon d’Or. He follows in the footsteps of Kevin Keegan, who also played in the Bundesliga, and Michael Owen, the last Englishman to lift the trophy for his country. Of course, all this supposes that Kane actually does win the Ballo n d’Or this year. He seems to be the favorite for the oddsmakers, but FC Barcelona and Spain youngster Lamine Yamal b oasts a strong claim thanks to his country winning the World Cup. Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappé has also put his name in for contention, though he falls short of Kane on goals, and Yamal (plus Kane) on trophies. Lest we forget Michael Oli se, Kane’s teammate, who had an incredible season of his own. For Harry Kane, this ceremony could represen t the pinnacle of personal achievement—the exact thing he was looking for when he left Tottenham Hotspur back in 2023. If the judges chosen by France Football make the right choice, the England striker could add his name to an illustrious list, sol idifying his legacy as one of the greatest strikers in the sport.lustrious list, solidifying his legacy as one of the greatest strikers in the sport. item.title: Travis Kelce’s Kansas City teammate says ‘if I had a son, I’d want him to be just like him’
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs TE Travis Kelce is not only a legend on the field, but he is also a shining example of a good man to his teammates off the field. The 36-year-old Kelce has established himself as one of the most respected veterans in the NFL, hoping to win a fourth Super Bowl title with the Chiefs in the 2026 season. One of the key reinforcements the Chiefs made to their roster after a 6-11 season in 2025 was rookie CB Mansoor Delane, who they selected with the No. 6 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Despite playing on opposite ends of the field, Kelce has left an impact on Delane. Mansoor Delane wishes his unborn son grows up to be like Travis Kelce In a mic’d-up moment from the Chiefs’ Week 6 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, rookie CB Delane was caught on audio praising his veteran teammate, wishing that if he had a son, he would grow up to be like Kelce. “If I had a son, I’d want him to be just like him. He’s got so much aura, bro” Kelce has been a model leader in the Chiefs’ locker room, with his work ethic and continued success setting a fantastic example for the young players. His success on and off the field also explains why a 22-year-old like Delane would want to have a son like him. But with Kelce being a world-famous athlete who is a multimillionaire and considered a gentleman, it’s hard to question anyone who says they want their son to be like Kelce. Kelce has picked up 20 receptions for 299 yards this season and has converted two touchdowns in a season where his connection with Mahomes is no longer required to be the driving force behind the Chiefs’ success. Delane has been a standout defensive rookie for the Chiefs, playing four games for 22 tackles (15 solo, seven assisted), two TFLs, one interception, and three passes defended. item.title: Sophie Cunningham questions Angel Reese’s play during the WNBA postseason
item.description: Source: lev radin/Shutterstock.com galecophoto/Depositphotos Cunningham questions Reese’s physical play Sophie Cunningham’s comments about Angel Reese’s physical play during the 2026 WNBA playoffs sparked debate about player safety and officiating. On her No Hesitation podcast, Cunningham discussed several incidents from the Atlanta Dream’s semifinal series against the New York Liberty, including exchanges involving Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones. Reese also played a key role in Atlanta’s sweep, scoring 22 points in the decisive Game 3 victory. The discussion highlights differing views on physical play, competitive intensity, and the consistency with which officials should enforce the rules. Depositphotos Reese helped Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals Atlanta defeated New York 85–83 in Game 3 of the semifinals on October 9, completing a three-game sweep. Reese scored 22 points in the deciding game at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, helping Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. The Dream entered the championship series unbeaten in the 2026 postseason after winning their first five playoff games. lev radin/Shutterstock.com Cunningham acknowledged Reese’s loyalty to teammates Cunningham did not dismiss Reese’s competitive approach entirely during the podcast discussion. She praised the Atlanta forward for supporting her teammates and noted that her intensity reflected care for those around her. However, Cunningham drew a distinction between standing up for a teammate and actions she believed could endanger opponents. Her criticism focused on specific plays rather than Reese’s effort alone. galkin57/Depositphotos The Sabrina Ionescu confrontation drew attention One incident involved New York Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu during the decisive semifinal game. After Ionescu was called for an offensive foul on a screen involving Atlanta guard Isobel Borlase, Reese followed Ionescu down the court and appeared to address her. Cunningham argued that the interaction should have resulted in a technical foul against Reese, although officials did not assess one. Dziurek/Depositphotos Cunningham questioned the technical foul decision Cunningham said she believed Reese should have received a technical foul for following Ionescu and speaking directly to her after the whistle. She argued that similar conduct would ordinarily draw a penalty during the regular season or other playoff games. The officials did not issue a technical foul to Reese for that exchange, making the decision a central point in Cunningham’s public criticism. steho/Depositphotos Jonquel Jones and Reese received technical fouls Another heated moment occurred after New York center Jonquel Jones blocked Reese’s shot near the basket. On her No Hesitation podcast, Cunningham discussed several incidents from the Atlanta Dream’s semifinal series against the New York Liberty, including exchanges involving Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones. The discussion highlights differing views on physical play, competitive intensity, and the consistency with which officials should enforce the rules. Depositphotos Reese helped Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals Atlanta defeated New York 85–83 in Game 3 of the semifinals on October 9, completing a three-game sweep. Reese scored 22 points in the deciding game at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, helping Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. The Dream entered the championship series unbeaten in the 2026 postseason after winning their first five playoff games. lev radin/Shutterstock.com Cunningham acknowledged Reese’s loyalty to teammates Cunningham did not dismiss Reese’s competitive approach entirely during the podcast discussion. She praised the Atlanta forward for supporting her teammates and noted that her intensity reflected care for those around her. However, Cunningham drew a distinction between standing up for a teammate and actions she believed could endanger opponents. Her criticism focused on specific plays rather than Reese’s effort alone. galkin57/Depositphotos The Sabrina Ionescu confrontation drew attention One incident involved New York Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu during the decisive semifinal game. After Ionescu was called for an offensive foul on a screen involving Atlanta guard Isobel Borlase, Reese followed Ionescu down the court and appeared to address her. Cunningham argued that the interaction should have resulted in a technical foul against Reese, although officials did not assess one. Dziurek/Depositphotos Cunningham questioned the technical foul decision Cunningham said she believed Reese should have received a technical foul for following Ionescu and speaking directly to her after the whistle. She argued that similar conduct would ordinarily draw a penalty during the regular season or other playoff games. The officials did not issue a technical foul to Reese for that exchange, making the decision a central point in Cunningham’s public criticism. steho/Depositphotos Jonquel Jones and Reese received technical fouls Another heated moment occurred after New York center Jonquel Jones blocked Reese’s shot near the basket. The two players exchanged words and made chest-to-chest contact before officials intervened. Both players received technical fouls during the game, according to the game recap. Cunningham said she wished neither player had received a technical foul, describing the exchange as part of competitive playoff basketball. galecophoto/Depositphotos Cunningham raised concerns about player safety Cunningham also discussed physical plays involving Reese and opposing players during the semifinal game. She objected to what she described as actions directed toward opponents’ knees and ankles, as well as contact involving a player in the air. Cunningham characterized those types of plays as dangerous, presenting her concerns as a matter of player safety rather than simply competitive trash talk. Interesting fact : Sophie Cunningham played college basketball at the University of Missouri . Featureflash/Depositphotos Breanna Stewart was involved in another disputed play New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart was involved in another play discussed by Cunningham and Drew Hanlen on their podcast. Cunningham criticized Reese for bumping Stewart to the floor after the play had ended. She also questioned why officials did not call a foul on that contact. Her comments were part of a broader discussion about the consistency of officiating during Atlanta’s semifinal series against New York. Interesting fact : The Atlanta Dream set a franchise scoring record in June 2026. katatonia82/Depositphotos Officiating consistency became part of the debate Cunningham’s remarks extended beyond whether Reese should have received a technical foul for confronting Ionescu. She questioned why officials penalized some exchanges but allowed other physical interactions to continue without a similar call. Her argument centered on consistent enforcement of the rules throughout a game. The discussion did not establish that officials had formally admitted to making an error on either play. steho/Depositphotos Reese delivered a strong performance in Game 3 Despite the attention surrounding the disputed plays, Reese also made a significant contribution to Atlanta’s victory. She scored 22 points in the deciding game as the Dream defeated the Liberty 85–83. Her performance helped Atlanta complete the three-game sweep and reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. The victory secured the Dream’s place in the championship series after an unbeaten start to the 2026 postseason. livephotosport/Depositphotos Atlanta completed a three-game semifinal sweep The Dream won the opening game of the semifinal series 92-82 on October 4, then took Game 2 by a score of 101-98 on October 7. Their 85-83 victory in Game 3 completed the sweep against New York. Atlanta’s run ended the Liberty’s postseason campaign and sent the Dream into the championship round with a 5-0 playoff record. galecophoto/Depositphotos The Dream advanced to face the Valkyries Atlanta’s semifinal victory set up a WNBA Finals matchup against the Golden State Valkyries. Golden State also swept its semifinal series, defeating the defending champion Las Vegas Aces to reach the championship round in its second season. The Finals began on October 17, 2026, giving both franchises an opportunity to pursue their first WNBA championship. Michael Porter Jr.’s comments have drawn attention to the ongoing conversations surrounding Cunningham and her role with the Indiana Fever. Explore Michael Porter Jr. sharing a pointed message about Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham . Mircea Moira/Depositphotos Cunningham’s comments kept Reese in the spotlight Cunningham’s podcast remarks brought renewed attention to Reese’s physical style of play just before Atlanta’s championship series. Her comments addressed specific incidents, including exchanges with Ionescu and Jones, as well as broader concerns about contact and officiating. Reese’s postseason production and Atlanta’s successful run remained important parts of the story, while Cunningham’s criticism represented her assessment of the plays rather than an official league ruling. Indiana faces important roster questions as the franchise prepares for the next stage of its WNBA campaign. item.title: Yankees Castoff Joins Hated Rival Immediate After Season Ends
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - APRIL 29: A view of the New York Yankees logo on a ball bag before the game against the Baltimore Orioles at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on April 29, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) Getty Images The New York Yankees are entering an important winter after another disappointing postseason exit, and the organization’s options for significant change just shrunk after it officially brought manager Aaron Boone back for another season. Attention now turns toward the possibility of big roster changes that can help New York get further into October next year after a particularly painful end to the Yankees’ season. “Boone is coming off one of the biggest disappointments of his tenure as Yankees manager — an embarrassing three-game sweep by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series,” Brendan Kuty and Chris Kirschner noted for The Athletic . And while the Yankees consider how to improve their major-league roster, one player who was cast off at the beginning of the ill-fated campaign has already secured his next opportunity with an American League East rival. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets’ $17 Million Castoff Sends 5-Word Yankees Message New York Yankees Castoff Signs With Division Rival Baltimore Orioles Left-hander Jayvien Sandridge has agreed to a minor-league contract with the Baltimore Orioles for the 2027 season, according to Matt Weyrich of The Baltimore Sun . Sandridge’s return to Baltimore marks another turn in a winding professional journey. The Orioles originally selected him in the 32nd round of the 2018 MLB Draft, and he spent time in their organization before moving through the Cincinnati Reds, San Diego Padres and Yankees systems. New York designated Sandridge for assignment in January 2026 and traded him to the Los Angeles Angels for cash considerations. The Angels later designated him for assignment as well, and Baltimore acquired him in another cash deal in March. “Sandridge, 28 in February, began 2026 on the Yankees’ roster,” Darragh McDonald wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . “He was designated for assignment in January and then flipped to the Angels for cash. The Halos designated him for assignment at the end of spring training. That led to another cash deal, this one sending him to Baltimore.” The new agreement keeps Sandridge with the Orioles organization after an injury-shortened 2026 campaign. He made six relief appearances for Triple-A Norfolk before landing on the injured list in early May. The Halos designated him for assignment at the end of spring training. He made six relief appearances for Triple-A Norfolk before landing on the injured list in early May. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Veteran Backstop Cuts Ties With Team Immediately After Season Ends Former New York Yankees Pitcher Looks For New Chance With AL East Rival Sandridge has limited major-league experience to draw on. He made his MLB debut with the Yankees on July 5, 2025, against the New York Mets, recording two outs while allowing two earned runs. His minor-league record offers a more complicated picture. The left-hander has demonstrated strikeout ability, but control has been a recurring concern, making his next opportunity dependent on both his health and his ability to limit walks. For Baltimore, the minor-league deal represents a low-risk way to retain a left-handed arm with some swing-and-miss potential. Sandridge will have to earn his way back into the major-league picture, rather than receiving a guaranteed roster spot. For the Yankees, his return to a division rival is a modest offseason footnote rather than a major roster blow. Still, with New York looking to move beyond its latest playoff disappointment, even smaller personnel moves help illustrate how quickly former Yankees can find new opportunities elsewhere in the division.
