item.content:encoded: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 09: Jeremy Hecklinski #10 of the Iowa Hawkeyes celebrates a touchdown against the Washington Huskies during the first half at Husky Stadium on October 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before we jump in to this week’s edition of Kirk Speaks, a quick shout out to our usual author Matt Cabel who welcomed in the newest addition to his household a week earlier than expected. Everyone is doing great, except for those of us who sit around waiting for him to digest these weekly pressers for us. So congrats to Matt and family – we’ll do our best to fill the void! Happy Floyd week, folks. The bye is behind us, the Hawkeyes sit at 5-1 and #15 in the country at the exact halfway point of the season and the biggest question in Iowa City got itself answered on a Tuesday afternoon: Jeremy Hecklinski is the starting quarterback Saturday at Minnesota. What I love most is HOW the news came out. Monday’s depth chart had the dreaded “OR” between Hank Brown and Hecklinski, everybody spent 24 hours reading tea leaves, and then Kirk just… mentioned it. Mid-answer. Almost to himself. The man has guarded quarterback decisions like state secrets for a quarter century and this one he dropped like he was reading a grocery list. Let’s get into the details. You can check out the full transcript HERE , my highlights and commentary below. Q. I think we know how much equity matters to you within the program, the day-by-day work. You have two quarterbacks that have gone on the road in tough environments and pulled out wins. Whoever you go with at quarterback on Saturday, how do you balance continuing to instill confidence in them but also understanding that, as you’ve mentioned, you have depth at quarterback. I don’t want to use the phrase is the leash going to be shorter if they don’t perform, but how do you kind of maintain that balance of instilling confidence and maybe looking to make a change? KIRK FERENTZ: We’ll handle that as we go. Did I put up the depth chart? So Hecklinski will be our starter Saturday. Since the start of the season, it’s been even. What’s good for us is they’ve both done good jobs and both won on the road in tough circumstances. So that gives us a lot of encouragement. I think we have two good quarterbacks, which a couple years ago we couldn’t say that. “Did I put up the depth chart?” is an all-time way to announce your starting quarterback. No statement, no graphic, just Kirk wondering aloud what’s on his own two-deep. Then casually announcing something completely counter to that depth chart after confirming it’s been put out. Wild, wild sequence and genuinely shocking that he announced anything at all. I’ve been pretty confident if Heck got the nod it would be under the guise that Hank Brown, while medically cleared and available as an emergency backup, was not fully back and needed more time. WELP…. Q. What is it that led you guys to the decision to start Jeremy? And then also is Hank at 100 percent? How is he doing health-wise? KIRK FERENTZ: Hank is 100 percent. He could have played the last game, emergency, but I don’t think it was a smart play to play him, and probably would have – not endangered him or they wouldn’t have cleared him, but probably would have set him back for a while. He’s perfectly healthy. A little sore last week, and having that bye week came at a good time. As a determining factor, it’s kind of like the first time. It’s not a coin toss, but it’s awfully close. Both guys, you can make an argument either way that makes sense. We just decided that was the best thing at this time to do, and we’ll just keep playing forward here. This part is maybe more baffling than Kirk just blurting it out. Brown is healthy – fully, 100 percent healthy, per KF – and the job went to Heck anyway. That makes this a performance call, not an injury bridge and that’s a big deal given where Iowa’s offense has been this season. When someone asked the question even more directly, Kirk made Brown’s case for him – “do you discount a quarterback bringing us back for two touchdowns in the fourth quarter?” – which tells you how close this really was . But close only counts in horseshoes. Heck’s the guy. Completing 79% of your throws against Power 4 defenses will do that for a guy. Q. Was curious with Xavier Styles, how you’ve seen him kind of develop since he got on campus and what he did to earn that starting opportunity? Also, I know you said Tyler Brown is out. Styles, do you expect him to start again versus Minnesota? KIRK FERENTZ: Kind of ties in with what Tom asked earlier about who’s going to — we’ve liked Xavier. Didn’t think he was ready. Anyway, with Tyler out, we have to find an answer. He and Anthony have both been competing. We just made that decision that last game to throw him in there and see what he’d do. He really flashed at some good things. Some detail work to take care of, which is what you’d expect any time a new player goes in. He’s only been here however many months, ten months on campus, so he’s still has some finer things. His knowledge base compared to like Zach Lutmer’s is a little bit different. Like his attitude and the way he runs around. He made a good showing for himself that first time out, so we’ll keep building on that. We’re going to keep working with Anthony too because he’s going to be a good player. The thing that both those guys are fighting is newness to the system and just all the intricate details. Luckily, we’ve got Zach back there to help quarterback some stuff and carry some of that burden. We liked what we saw. Just even standing on the sidelines a couple weeks ago, just him flashing around, you can just get a feel sometimes, like this guy is trying to make some plays and get involved and be active. Be curious to see where it goes. It’s all in front of him right now. Same thing with Anthony. He’ll get his chance. This feels like another one of Kirk’s meandering non-answers, but I think it roundabout highlights what makes Phil Parker’s defense click. We see the same basic defense that is predictable but there are details and intricacies that are nuanced and barely noticeable to the untrained eye. And the critical piece is everyone executing their role without the need to process. That’s a tough ask for a young guy and getting reps for so many of these younger players should pay big dividends down the road. Just hope it doesn’t bite the Hawks against quality QBs – Minnesota’s Drake Lindsay is capable of making Iowa pay for mistakes in the back end. Q. Also, when they went to Purdue, you could tell there was almost an it’s just Purdue kind of attitude with the way they played. What kind of message do you tell them and how they evaluate the film and the results in order to prepare them for this game? KIRK FERENTZ: One side thought, the just Purdue thing, which is kind of a commentary on last weekend. When my kids were all younger, it’s the old – I was guilty of the same thing when I was a little kid. When you play Little League games, right? The Cubs beat the Tigers, and then the Tigers beat the Reds, hey, we beat the Tigers, so we’ll naturally beat this team, and you end up losing by 10 runs. That kind of thinking gets you beat. Then the bigger picture is last weekend is a great illustration, if anyone is paying attention – I’m thinking more about our players than everybody else – but it’s just week to week because you can’t make it make sense if you do comparative scores. The Little League transitive-property bit is Kirk at his Kirkiest. The annoying part is he’s right. Minnesota beat the two ranked teams it played and got blown out by two unranked ones, so comparative scores are useless here. He also got in a swipe at the sport’s December brain – the “playoff shows coming out sometime in the next four weeks” – and said the best advice he can give his guys is to just worry about Saturday. We, of course, are unde

item.title: Future Hogs Week 7: College football players who could help the Commanders
item.description: LUBBOCK, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 18: Amare Thomas #0 of the Houston Cougars runs with the ball during the second half of the game against the Texas Tech Red Raiders at Galaxy Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Lubbock, Texas. (Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images What an unpredictable week in college football. #1 Georgia lost to an unranked Auburn team, and #2 Notre Dame lost late to #8 BYU. #3 Miami needed overtime to beat in-state rival Florida State. #4 Ohio State won a competitive matchup over #5 Indiana, handing them their first loss at home under head coach Curt Cignetti. #6 Alabama lost by a wide margin in Knoxville to #14 Tennessee, and #7 Texas gave up a lead and lost to unranked Florida. This chaos has resulted in no undefeated SEC teams, UCLA as the only unbeaten team in the Big Ten, and three undefeated Big 12 teams – BYU, Texas Tech, and Utah – in the top 10. Week 8 will see one of those unbeaten teams in the Big 12, #10 Utah, facing off against #14 Houston. A new entrant into the top 10, #9 UCLA will host Michigan State. Both #13 Alabama and #17 Texas will try to avoid three losses in a row. The Crimson Tide will play Texas A&M while the Longhorns play #7 Ole Miss. The top team in the country, Miami, will host Pittsburgh. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. Ashton Daniels | QB | Senior | Florida State As a developmental quarterback prospect, Ashton Daniels could be a fit in Washington. He’s got the size for the position at 6’2”, 225 pounds. He’s not the most creative runner at the position, but he can run away from, and at that size, even over defenders. As a passer, Daniels has shown the ability to make NFL-level throws between defenders and into tight windows. He also can put touch on his passes and allow receivers to run underneath them. He can get himself into trouble when he tries to force throws thinking he can beat defenders. Daniels has thrown 8 interceptions this season. If the Commanders think they can help him improve his decision making, he might be worth investing in. In an overtime loss to Miami, Daniels went 15 of 28 for 298 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception on the last play of the game which any Florida State fan will argue was a catch. He also added 31 yards and a touchdown on the ground. As a bonus for those who want a big receiver, check out Daniels’ teammate, the 6’6”, 230 pound wide receiver Duce Robinson, in the clip below. He’s wearing #0. DeSean Bishop | RB | Senior | Tennessee Many hoped that Kaytron Allen would be the Commanders’ short yardage back. That didn’t happen. DeSean Bishop can be that and more. He isn’t a flashy runner that will wow you with elite speed, burst, or elusiveness. What Bishop is at 5’10”, 215 pounds is a rugged back that will deliver consistent punishment to a defense, wearing them down as the game progresses.
item.content:encoded: LUBBOCK, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 18: Amare Thomas #0 of the Houston Cougars runs with the ball during the second half of the game against the Texas Tech Red Raiders at Galaxy Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Lubbock, Texas. (Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images What an unpredictable week in college football. #1 Georgia lost to an unranked Auburn team, and #2 Notre Dame lost late to #8 BYU. #3 Miami needed overtime to beat in-state rival Florida State. #4 Ohio State won a competitive matchup over #5 Indiana, handing them their first loss at home under head coach Curt Cignetti. #6 Alabama lost by a wide margin in Knoxville to #14 Tennessee, and #7 Texas gave up a lead and lost to unranked Florida. The top team in the country, Miami, will host Pittsburgh. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. Ashton Daniels | QB | Senior | Florida State As a developmental quarterback prospect, Ashton Daniels could be a fit in Washington. He’s got the size for the position at 6’2”, 225 pounds. He’s not the most creative runner at the position, but he can run away from, and at that size, even over defenders. As a passer, Daniels has shown the ability to make NFL-level throws between defenders and into tight windows. He also can put touch on his passes and allow receivers to run underneath them. He can get himself into trouble when he tries to force throws thinking he can beat defenders. Daniels has thrown 8 interceptions this season. If the Commanders think they can help him improve his decision making, he might be worth investing in. In an overtime loss to Miami, Daniels went 15 of 28 for 298 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception on the last play of the game which any Florida State fan will argue was a catch. He also added 31 yards and a touchdown on the ground. As a bonus for those who want a big receiver, check out Daniels’ teammate, the 6’6”, 230 pound wide receiver Duce Robinson, in the clip below. He’s wearing #0. DeSean Bishop | RB | Senior | Tennessee Many hoped that Kaytron Allen would be the Commanders’ short yardage back. That didn’t happen. DeSean Bishop can be that and more. He isn’t a flashy runner that will wow you with elite speed, burst, or elusiveness. What Bishop is at 5’10”, 215 pounds is a rugged back that will deliver consistent punishment to a defense, wearing them down as the game progresses. His superpower is his ability to run through tackles and gain tough yardage, a role the Commanders need filled desperately. As a former walk-on, it is easy to root for Bishop’s success at the next level. Bishop rushed 32 times for 159 yards and two touchdows in the Volunteers’ victory over Alabama. DeSean Bishop’s Ranks Among RBs from Week 7: 🟠 121 Yards AFTER Contact (1st) 🟠 13 Missed Tackles Forced (1st) @Vol_Football pic.twitter.com/FF2lIwJgit — PFF College (@PFF_College) October 18, 2026 Amare Thomas | WR | Senior | Houston It was tough to see Terry McLaurin sustain a torn patellar tendon against San Francisco. The injury makes the need to improve the position group more urgent than it already was. Houston’s Amare Thomas is a receiver who could really improve the receiving corps. The 6’0”, 205 pound wideout is a quick-twitch athlete who can create separation with his route running. His superior body control and above-average hands allow him to make catches outside the frame of his body. After the catch, Thomas has contact balance to break arm tackles. Long speed is a bit of a question. Thomas helped Houston outlast Oklahoma State with seven catches for 126 yards and two touchdowns. Houston WR Amare Thomas is an NFL WR playing in the Big 12 He had a huge week 7 vs Oklahoma State with 7 receptions, 127 yards, and 2 TDs The size (6'0 205), body control, route running, and ability after the catch remind me of DJ Moore pic.twitter.com/Bs0lBaqgSS — Draft Capital Podcast (@TheDraftCapital) October 19, 2026 Peter Clarke | TE | Senior | Temple I talked about Peter Clarke during this time last year and it looks like he has gotten better. He’s a huge player at 6’6”, 265 pounds, and he uses that size in a variety of ways. First, it allows him to be an effective blocker at the line of scrimmage. Clarke looks like he has improved his technique and is getting lower to maintain leverage. He’s also added more to his game as a receiver. There’s more diversity to the routes he runs, but he still shows the quickness and speed of a smaller player. Clarke became Temple’s all-time touchdown leader for tight ends in a loss to Charlotte with 123 yards and a touchdown on five catches. Peter Clarke with a record breaking touchdown 🥳 📺 | @ESPNCFB #BuiltToRise x @Temple_FB pic.twitter.com/HqSFrMMPEV — The American (@American_Conf) October 17, 2026 Temple TE Peter Clarke ( @iam_peterclarke ) had his best game last week vs UConn. Clarke caught 5 passes for 88 yards and a TD. #TempleTUFF pic.twitter.com/2yQ3LlxZaa — Bryan (@RealBGauvin23) October 17, 2026 Justin Evans| C | Senior | Nebraska The offensive line had its fair share of struggles against the 49ers. Justin Evans looks like an immediate upgrade at the center position. He has a compact, powerful body at 6’2”, 315 pounds. Evans snaps the ball and gets his hands onto defenders quickly. He is stout in pass protection, constantly moving his feet to mirror rushers. Evans has a solid anchor to prevent power rushers from going through him to get to the quarterback. One of my favorite traits of his is he’ll constantly look for defenders to block. In the run game, he’s not a people mover. What he’ll do is identify defenders and sustain his block. Nebraska used a power run game, so Evans may not be a great fit for a zone rushing attack. Nebraska suffered a close loss on the road to Oregon, but #51 below had a good game. Justin Evans (6’2 315) Nebraska ✅ 10 pressures and 0 sacks allowed during the 2025 season ✅ Extensive experience at both left guard and center ✅ Finishing mentality ✅ 1,900 career snaps played entering the 2026 season ✅ 84.0 pass blocking grade in 2025 ✅ 75.0 run blocking… pic.twitter.com/bnT1U5Cxih — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) June 11, 2026 A.J. Holmes, Jr. | DT | Senior | Texas Tech The Commanders blitz at a high rate, but they need players that can win one-on-one matchups and finish plays behind the line of scrimmage. A.J. Holmes, Jr. is one of the best defensive tackles in the country. His game starts with his power. He gets off the ball quickly and into blockers before they can get hands on him. He can walk them back into the quarterback or shed them to make plays. He is also a disciplined player that keeps gap integrity, understanding his role in the defense. He is a high-motor player that doesn’t give up on plays. Holmes, Jr. finished Texas Tech’s win over Arizona State with five tackles and 1.5 sacks. "Anytime you see a big man in a little man's number, you know that's a BAAAAAAAD man." – @RGIII AJ Holmes with the HUGE third-down stop for @TexasTechFB pic.twitter.com/VWWvc6MlDJ — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) October 17, 2026 Ben Roberts | LB | Senior | Texas Tech Playing behind A.J. Holmes, Jr. are a few talented linebackers. Ben Roberts is the one who stood out this week. Where many linebackers are getting smaller, Roberts is 6’3”, 245 lbs, but he can move at that size. He’s not a sideline-to-sideline player, but he covers g

item.title: Indiana football must solve running game woes to reach its goals this season
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Indiana Hoosiers running back Turbo Richard (1) lines up behind the line of scrimmage in the second half of play during a college football game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Indiana Hoosiers on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of Indiana football’s supposed strengths just two weeks ago has emerged as perhaps its biggest weakness after a pair of lackluster showings. The Hoosiers’ running game looked great two games into Big Ten play. Indiana ran for 6.8 yards per carry as a team against Northwestern with Lee Beebe Jr. taking over for an injured Turbo Richard, logging 203 yards on 24 carries to average 8.5 on the ground in large part thanks to a 70-yard burst in the fourth quarter. It looked even better the next week when the Hoosiers averaged 8.4 yards per carry with Richard turning 13 carries into 204 yards for a blistering 15.7 yards per carry. Ever since? Nothing remotely close. Windy conditions made the run crucial at Nebraska and the Cornhuskers knew it, committing extensive resources to stopping the Hoosiers on the ground. Indiana, which had seen two different backs eclipse 200 rushing yards in the previous two weeks, managed just 65 rushing yards as a team and just 3 yards per carry against that defense. On top of that, Indiana lost the time of possession battle and just didn’t run that many offensive plays. It was a combination of Josh Hoover’s arm and processing alongside Nick Marsh’s playmaking that won that game. This seemed a potential outlier at the time. Weird game, weird weather. Whatever. Then came the massive matchup against Ohio State at home where Indiana ran into the same issue, literally. The Hoosiers managed just 73 yards on the ground and just 2.5 per carry against the Buckeyes as Turbo Richard finished with 46 and Beebe Jr. with 24. Neither were explosive, with their longest rushes on the game being tied at just seven yards. Despite the criticism he’s received, including from this very blog, it was Hoover that kept Indiana in position to win that game at the end. Indiana’s running game was doing it no favors. So, what gives? How did Indiana go from this explosive attack to looking pedestrian at best in just two weeks? It isn’t a talent issue in the backfield. Richard and Beebe Jr. have both proven capable, this very season and in the past, of putting together strong performances on the ground. item.content:encoded: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Indiana Hoosiers running back Turbo Richard (1) lines up behind the line of scrimmage in the second half of play during a college football game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Indiana Hoosiers on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of Indiana football’s supposed strengths just two weeks ago has emerged as perhaps its biggest weakness after a pair of lackluster showings. The Hoosiers’ running game looked great two games into Big Ten play. Indiana ran for 6.8 yards per carry as a team against Northwestern with Lee Beebe Jr. taking over for an injured Turbo Richard, logging 203 yards on 24 carries to average 8.5 on the ground in large part thanks to a 70-yard burst in the fourth quarter. It looked even better the next week when the Hoosiers averaged 8.4 yards per carry with Richard turning 13 carries into 204 yards for a blistering 15.7 yards per carry. Ever since? Nothing remotely close. Windy conditions made the run crucial at Nebraska and the Cornhuskers knew it, committing extensive resources to stopping the Hoosiers on the ground. Indiana, which had seen two different backs eclipse 200 rushing yards in the previous two weeks, managed just 65 rushing yards as a team and just 3 yards per carry against that defense. On top of that, Indiana lost the time of possession battle and just didn’t run that many offensive plays. It was a combination of Josh Hoover’s arm and processing alongside Nick Marsh’s playmaking that won that game. This seemed a potential outlier at the time. Weird game, weird weather. Whatever. Then came the massive matchup against Ohio State at home where Indiana ran into the same issue, literally. The Hoosiers managed just 73 yards on the ground and just 2.5 per carry against the Buckeyes as Turbo Richard finished with 46 and Beebe Jr. with 24. Neither were explosive, with their longest rushes on the game being tied at just seven yards. Despite the criticism he’s received, including from this very blog, it was Hoover that kept Indiana in position to win that game at the end. Indiana’s running game was doing it no favors. So, what gives? How did Indiana go from this explosive attack to looking pedestrian at best in just two weeks? It isn’t a talent issue in the backfield. Richard and Beebe Jr. have both proven capable, this very season and in the past, of putting together strong performances on the ground. Their individual performances against Northwestern and Rutgers weren’t fools gold, that was just players making plays. To really break this down you have to go back to this past offseason when Indiana reloaded its backfield through the transfer portal and returned a key piece from injury. Mike Shanahan and Curt Cignetti’s offense has changed some over the years as different players have come and gone and it’s certainly been friendly for quarterbacks, but everything starts with the run. That’s just football in general, but humor me for a moment. Indiana’s rushing attack in 2024 and 2025, particularly the latter season, was an efficiency-focused operation. The Hoosiers’ offense was so effective last season because Roman Hemby and Kaelon Black, both powerful downhill runners, could be relied on to pick up 4 or so yards on any given run. Do that enough and opposing defensive coordinators have to respond, trying to create tackles for loss and stuffs by committing more resources to the run. That opens up the pass and you get plays like all of those deep shots to Charlie Becker throughout the postseason. There was a shift this past offseason that probably should’ve been immediately apparent when Indiana added Richard, a different kind of back than the program usually leans on. Indiana found success with those powerful efficiency runners like Hemby, Black and Ty Son Lawton, with some burst from Justice Ellison, but Richard was used as an explosive weapon at Boston College. The Hoosiers wanted to get more explosive on the ground. Richard was obviously the focal point and took over immediately as Indiana’s lead back but Beebe Jr. was pretty explosive in his limited attempts in 2025 and had long runs during his time at UAB. Indiana seemed to lean into this, trying to put its personnel in position to do what they do best For a while, that obviously worked. The Hoosiers had one of the most explosive ground games in the sport heading into the Ohio State matchup even after the Nebraska debacle: Most Explosive Offenses 🏈 pic.twitter.com/4FL8IvY4Vv — Cody Nagel (@CodyNagel247) October 11, 2026 Now, not so much. What changed? Well, Indiana’s non-running back personnel and the caliber of opponent it was up against. Indiana lost its starting center and right tackle this past offseason with both Pat Coogan and Kahlil Benson moving onto the NFL. Not only that, tight end Riley Nowakowski departed for the professional ranks as well. That’s multiple key blockers gone. Indiana replaced Coogan by sliding right guard Bray Lynch over to the center spot, making way for Wisconsin transfer Joe Brunner to slide in at the latter’s vacant spot. Adedamola Ajani, who took extensive snaps in the postseason, took over at right tackle. Indiana opted for a few more interesting moves at tight end, adding Brock Schott as a sophomore transfer out of Miami in an already inexperienced room. Indiana added just one experienced piece to fill this select gap in Brunner. The remainder of the moves were either shuffling, rising depth or adding another inexperienced piece. One way or another, these players aren’t performing at the standard set by their predecessors. Lynch, sorry to say, was probably the weaker link on last year’s offensive line. That’s not necessarily awful, the rest of them are either in the NFL or will be soon. It’s also a problem when all of a sudden he’s at the line’s most critical position when it comes to the run. Coogan brought a ton of experience and leadership not only on the offensive line, but to playing center. He’d just helped lead Notre Dame’s offensive line to the National Championship Game. His was going to be a tough act to follow. Indiana is running through the middle of its line, just like last year. Unlike last year, it’s weaker, so it’s finding less success. This wasn’t apparent against the fronts fielded by Northwestern and Rutgers, giving Richard and Beebe Jr. greater room to work with. Against more talented groups at Nebraska and Ohio State? Indiana was physically overmatched and couldn’t get anything going. What could help here? Well, some schematic changes and more of an emphasis on the efficiency of yesteryear could change things, but the personnel isn’t as well built for that either as it was in 2025. The return of Khobie Martin, a back more in that mold, could ail the issue. One way or another, Indiana has to figure out how to run the ball. Soon. Michigan is looming as another tough, big defensive front that’s poised to give the Hoosiers issues.

item.title: NFLPA demands full investigation into Eagles’ care of QB Jalen Hurts
item.description: Two of the NFL’s top health officials backed the Philadelphia Eagles ‘ handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots at the league’s fall meeting in New York on Tuesday. By that night, the NFL Players Association had called for a full investigation and raised a problem with the league’s own account of the case. Specialists in London found a clot in Hurts’ left calf on Oct. 10, which the Eagles first described as a “left calf superficial vein thrombosis.” The team’s medical staff and independent doctors concluded he “could safely play” against the Jacksonville Jaguars the next day, and Hurts played the full game in a 19-17 loss. A follow-up ultrasound back in Philadelphia on Oct. 14 showed the clot had moved. On Monday, the Eagles and Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, disclosed a deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning clots had reached both lungs. Hurts is on injured reserve and is expected to miss the rest of the season, though the team said in its joint statement with Lynn that it anticipates “no long-term effects.” Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images What the NFL said about the Eagles’ doctors “I don’t think you can take that outcome and say there was something flawed about the process,” NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills told reporters . Sills described the Eagles’ medical staff as “incredibly conservative and incredibly vigilant” and rejected the idea that football people had a hand in the decision. “Any idea or any suggestion that a team physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a general manager, a team owner, it just doesn’t happen,” Sills said. Jeff Miller, the NFL executive vice president who oversees player health and safety, called the criticism of the team’s doctors unfounded. “Conservative steps were taken to ensure Jalen Hurts’ health was always made the first priority and continues to be,” Miller said . Miller also said the league has “a complete understanding of the course of events,” built from conversations with the Eagles’ staff, the hospital in London and the doctors involved. The NFL declined to discuss the specifics of Hurts’ case, citing medical privacy, and The Athletic reported the league will not punish the Eagles. item.content:encoded: Two of the NFL’s top health officials backed the Philadelphia Eagles ‘ handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots at the league’s fall meeting in New York on Tuesday. By that night, the NFL Players Association had called for a full investigation and raised a problem with the league’s own account of the case. Specialists in London found a clot in Hurts’ left calf on Oct. 10, which the Eagles first described as a “left calf superficial vein thrombosis.” The team’s medical staff and independent doctors concluded he “could safely play” against the Jacksonville Jaguars the next day, and Hurts played the full game in a 19-17 loss. A follow-up ultrasound back in Philadelphia on Oct. 14 showed the clot had moved. On Monday, the Eagles and Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, disclosed a deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning clots had reached both lungs. Hurts is on injured reserve and is expected to miss the rest of the season, though the team said in its joint statement with Lynn that it anticipates “no long-term effects.” Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Sills described the Eagles’ medical staff as “incredibly conservative and incredibly vigilant” and rejected the idea that football people had a hand in the decision. “Any idea or any suggestion that a team physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a general manager, a team owner, it just doesn’t happen,” Sills said. Jeff Miller, the NFL executive vice president who oversees player health and safety, called the criticism of the team’s doctors unfounded. “Conservative steps were taken to ensure Jalen Hurts’ health was always made the first priority and continues to be,” Miller said . Miller also said the league has “a complete understanding of the course of events,” built from conversations with the Eagles’ staff, the hospital in London and the doctors involved. The NFL declined to discuss the specifics of Hurts’ case, citing medical privacy, and The Athletic reported the league will not punish the Eagles. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. item.title: The figures that show Mercedes has lost its supremacy in F1 2026
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes is confident it can win again in the 2026 Formula 1 season, but is aware it has been facing a bigger challenge than ever from the other top teams. The Silver Arrows triumphed in the opening six grands prix of the campaign, as F1 switched to new technical regulations. Later on, rival upgrades meant Ferrari claimed two victories in Austria and Great Britain, then McLaren ’s Lando Norris took back-to-back wins in Hungary and the Netherlands, and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen prevailed most recently in Malaysia and Singapore. Mercedes didn’t hold off from updating its car either, but the team is well aware its performance advantage has been slashed. That’s despite a healthy lead in both championships, with a maiden world title within reach of Kimi Antonelli in Austin. “I think we've sounded like a bit of a broken record all year, to be honest, because we've been saying how close and competitive this season is, even if we were able to put a good run of wins together earlier in the season,” deputy team principal Bradley Lord commented on the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show. “That is being borne out. “We saw Ferrari upgrading their car either prior to or up to Baku, Red Bull doing the same. We obviously brought our update to Malaysia and we've seen different levels of hitting the ground running, I guess, with those updates. Last two races, both Red Bull and Ferrari have been more competitive than they had been in the events up to then.” Average gap to pole position Australia to Japan Miami to Belgium Hungary to Singapore Hung. to Sing. Read Also: Why Mercedes switched George Russell to its old F1 car spec in Singapore To compound Mercedes’ issues, its latest W17 update has not delivered as much as it was hoping for relative to its rivals – hence very balanced performance among top teams and Red Bull’s return to victory. 2026 marks only the second time four outfits have taken several wins each (Mercedes 11, Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull two) since 1990, after the same outfits shone in 2024. So when asked who will be the team to beat in Austin, deputy technical director Simone Resta pondered: “It's quite interesting to see that in every weekend you go in, you are never sure about who's going to be the strongest one out there. “With what we've seen so far with Red Bull, they'll be there fighting for the top position for sure. They've been quite strong now in a few races and they will be strong. “We've seen a strong Ferrari more or less in all the conditions. Maybe they miss a little bit, let's say, to be in the top position, but they're very competitive. “And we need to respect McLaren. McLaren, they are the world champion team and they've shown in some races this year that they can be the strongest out there, even with some margin. “There's good possibility that all of these teams will be strong there, and it makes it even more exciting for ourselves. You will try to really squeeze out a bit more from the package, try to optimise our configuration and come back to the top again, like we were in Baku, like we were in Monza, like we've been able to win in Madrid. We can do it again.” Read Also: How can Kimi Antonelli become world champion at F1 US GP? To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Dallas Cowboys: Add Former 2nd-Round Pick to the Squad
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys could add a quarterback after losing Joe Milton III to the Philadelphia Eagles, which leaves them with only two on the roster. One injury to monitor is Dak Prescott , who suffered an apparent rib injury in Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers after taking a shot to the chest. Prescott finished the game, and Brian Schottenheimer told the media he didn’t need X-rays , had the wind knocked out of him, and that the injury was just a bruise. The Dallas Cowboys add a former 2nd-round pick to the squad Sep 29, 2024; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Kyle Trask (2) against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first half at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images According to Todd Archer of ESPN NFL Nation, the Cowboys have signed Kyle Trask to their practice squad, effectively replacing Joe Milton III as the team’s third-string quarterback. Trask can be elevated to the game-day roster three times without penalty; otherwise, a fourth elevation would require a promotion to the active roster. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ second-round pick is on his fourth team and entering his sixth NFL season. The Cowboys are signing QB Kyle Trask to their practice squad, per sources. He replaces Joe Milton III, who signed to the Eagles active roster last week. A second-round pick by Tampa Bay in 2021, he has also been with Atlanta and Carolina. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) October 20, 2026 The Buccaneers re-signed Kyle Trask to a one-year deal last offseason. Unfortunately, Trask lost the backup quarterback job to Teddy Bridgewater last season, prompting Tampa Bay to release him during roster cuts. He signed with the Falcons’ practice squad in November and spent the last two months there before his contract expired. The Panthers signed Trask in early August, but released him during roster cuts. He remained unsigned through the first six weeks of the regular season. More Cowboys news Nov 23, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; A general view of a Dallas Cowboys helmet before the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Why Dallas Cowboys CB Is on the Hot Seat Dallas Cowboys: Get Positive Update on Superstar for Week 6 The post Dallas Cowboys: Add Former 2nd-Round Pick to the Squad appeared first on Gridiron Heroics .

item.title: Anthony Davis says he was called out by a Wizards teammate who's 13 years younger than him
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Anthony Davis is one of the most accomplished players in the NBA, but his young Washington Wizards teammate Tre Johnson still called him out. The 33-year-old veteran is a 10-time All-Star and a former winner of the championship when he was with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020. You would imagine that young players wouldn’t dare question someone like him, but Johnson proved that everyone is equal in a team during a recent practice session. Anthony Davis says Tre Johnson called him out after a poor practice session Johnson is only a second-year pro with the Washington Wizards, but it is clear to see that he is fearless. The 20-year-old, who is 13 years younger than 33-year-old Davis, held the veteran accountable after he missed too many shots in practice. Everybody has a bad day, and when it’s someone who has achieved as much as Davis, you would imagine that his teammates would cut him some slack. However, Johnson mocked his senior teammate and claimed that he looked nothing like a Top 75 player during the practice session. Narrating the incident, Davis told Ben Strober on X : “One day I missed a lot of shots in practice, and Tre Johnson actually came to me, and he was like: ‘Hey, man, you weren’t Top 75 today.’ “You look for that type of stuff, with players who’ll hold you accountable no matter what you’ve done in this league and where you are in this league.” What Johnson did takes a lot of courage. Players of his age wouldn’t have dared to say anything of the sort to an accomplished senior professional in the previous generation. This, however, is a good thing, as every player needs to hold each other accountable if they are to achieve anything meaningful this season. Anthony Davis believes ‘people forgot’ who he is due to the past few NBA seasons

item.title: Uganda denies Ebola outbreak after Nigeria confirms imported case
item.description: Uganda has denied having an active Ebola outbreak following Nigeria’s confirmation of an imported case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), insisting that it has no confirmed active infections as authorities investigate where the patient contracted the virus. In a public statement issued in Kampala on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Uganda’s Ministry of Health said the Nigerian patient had travelled through the country before arriving in Nigeria but stressed that her transit did not establish where she was infected. “We wish to clarify that, as at the time of this statement, Uganda has NO confirmed active Ebola cases,” the ministry said. The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: We Call for Calm and Vigilance,” added that preliminary information indicated the woman had travelled through Uganda in early October without symptoms and developed them after arriving in Nigeria. “Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said. It added that Nigeria’s government was expected to provide detailed information about the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to support further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. The Ugandan authorities also said they were strengthening screening and public health controls at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies. Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, announced the confirmed case on Tuesday, saying laboratory tests had established that the woman was infected with Ebola virus disease. According to Pate, the patient had recently travelled to East Africa, including Uganda, before returning to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7. Her condition reportedly worsened four days later, prompting further medical attention and testing. The woman was admitted to a private hospital, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. She has since been isolated and is receiving medical care. Pate said health authorities had identified 44 contacts and commenced contact tracing to prevent further transmission. Surveillance has also been strengthened at Nigeria’s points of entry. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare is coordinating the response with the FCT Health Services Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and other public health partners. The minister urged public and private healthcare facilities to remain vigilant and maintain a high index of suspicion for possible Ebola cases, particularly among patients with relevant travel histories and compatible symptoms. He also urged Nigerians to remain calm, practise good hygiene and promptly seek medical attention if they experience symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. item.title: Real Madrid had already tried to sign blockbuster summer arrival back in 2025 – report
item.description: Real Madrid had already tried to sign blockbuster summer arrival back in 2025 – report Real Madrid reportedly explored a move for Yan Diomande in 2025, when the Ivorian attacker was still playing for Leganes, but abandoned the pursuit because of the number of wingers already available in the squad. According to El Mundo , the Spanish giants’ interest predated the forward’s breakthrough at the 2026 FIFA World Cup and his subsequent arrival at the Santiago Bernabeu. Diomande eventually joined Real Madrid from RB Leipzig in a deal worth €125 million plus a further €15 million in potential add-ons, signing a contract that runs until 2033. His recent impact against Sevilla, when he provided an assist and scored a stunning goal, has offered an early glimpse of why Real Madrid were determined to secure his signature. Real Madrid tracked Diomande before his rise to stardom Real Madrid’s interest in Diomande reportedly began before he became one of the most sought-after attacking prospects in European football. Real Madrid showed interest in Diomande when he was at Leganes. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The club opened negotiations when he was at Leganes, but the existing depth of options on the wings meant there was no clear pathway for him into the squad. Diomande instead moved to RB Leipzig, where he continued his development before attracting renewed attention from Europe’s leading clubs. According to El Mundo, Real Madrid’s earlier decision was driven by squad composition rather than a lack of interest in the player’s potential. And by the time Real Madrid returned to the race, Diomande’s performances had strengthened his reputation and increased the competition for his signature. World Cup performances reignite Madrid’s pursuit Diomande is now Real Madrid’s club-record signing. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The report indicates that Rodrygo’s injury helped push Real Madrid back into the transfer market, while Diomande’s impressive 2026 World Cup campaign reinforced the club’s conviction that he was worth pursuing. Paris Saint-Germain were also interested in the Ivorian, and Diomande had been close to joining the French club. Los Blancos’ intervention, however, changed the situation, with the attacker ultimately choosing the Spanish side instead. The resulting transfer carried an enormous financial commitment. At €125 million guaranteed, with up to €15 million in add-ons, Diomande arrived under the pressure that naturally accompanies a record-breaking signing.

item.title: NBTI announces $600m pipeline for Nigerian innovation
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI) has unveiled an investment and development-finance pipeline exceeding $600 million for solar energy and other development initiatives, following the participation of 298 Nigerian innovators at the NextGen Innovation Challenge 2026 in London. The proposed financing comprises a $500 million solar-energy programme for universities and polytechnics and a $100 million financing arrangement for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The funds, however, have not been confirmed as received or fully mobilised. Speaking at a world press conference on Wednesday, NBTI Director-General, Dr Kazeem Kolawole Raji, said the October 9 event, organised in partnership with UKALD, provided an international platform for showcasing Nigerian technologies and connecting innovators with investors and commercial partners. The number of participating innovators rose from 105 in 2025 to 298 this year, representing all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with innovations spanning agriculture, healthcare, artificial intelligence, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing. “Our innovators have demonstrated that Nigeria has ideas worthy of international attention. Our responsibility is to help create the conditions in which those ideas can grow, compete and deliver lasting value to our people,” Raji said. NBTI said discussions with Gigawatt Global focused on developing solar farms in universities and polytechnics under power purchase agreements, while a memorandum of understanding with Financial Innovation for Impact, UK, also known as Cambridge Investors, covered the proposed $100 million financing for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The initiative targets one million micro and small businesses for solar-energy solutions, 50,000 direct youth jobs and 10,000 trained field marketers, with ₦30 billion in blended financing targeted for its first phase. Other outcomes include an announced $100,000 investment commitment by Dubai-based investor Erin Grover for three women innovators and international acceleration opportunities valued at $160,000 for 16 selected innovators. The Learning and Development Bureau UK also offered leadership and management scholarships worth more than £80,000 collectively to the 16 innovators and pledged assistance with UK Global Talent Visa applications, subject to eligibility. Raji said the priority was now to turn the opportunities into viable businesses, jobs and measurable economic benefits, urging investors and development partners to support Nigerian innovators with funding, mentorship and market access. “Our focus must now move decisively from visibility to implementation, from promising concepts to commercially viable solutions, and from announcements to independently verifiable outcomes,” he said. The post NBTI announces $600m pipeline for Nigerian innovation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PANDEF mourns Uduaghan, hails his peacebuilding role
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has mourned the death of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, who died three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, described Uduaghan as an exceptional leader whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unwavering. Igali stated this in a condolence letter to Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on the death of the former governor, according to a statement issued on Wednesday. He praised Uduaghan for his significant contributions to peace and stability in the Niger Delta, particularly during his tenure as Secretary to the State Government and later as governor, when militancy was heightened across the region. In the letter, Igali said he was shocked by the news of Uduaghan’s death, describing the late governor as a close associate and personal friend. “I write to express my total shock at the news of the passing into glory of our dearly beloved brother, the former Governor of Delta State, HE Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan. Although we mourn, but we all hold strong belief that the Almighty God knows best, and we glorify His exalted name,” he said. Igali added that he and Uduaghan had maintained a cordial relationship since they served simultaneously as secretaries to their respective state governments. “Without doubt, he was an exceptional man through and through, whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unfettered,” he said. He noted that Uduaghan played a significant role in bringing peace and stability to the Niger Delta during a period of heightened militancy in the South-South region. Igali described the former governor’s death as a major loss not only to Delta State but also to the Niger Delta and Nigeria as a whole. He expressed hope that Uduaghan’s legacy of service to God and humanity would endure, saying the late governor had “embedded his name in gold in the annals of our history.” Igali also asked Oborevwori to convey his deepest condolences to the Uduaghan family and the people of Delta State, praying for the repose of the former governor’s soul. The post PANDEF mourns Uduaghan, hails his peacebuilding role appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Showunmi reaffirms commitment to Abiola’s legacy, national unity
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of the Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi has reaffirmed his commitment to Nigeria’s unity, democratic development and the ideals for which the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale (MKO) Abiola sacrificed his life, insisting that the struggle to actualise the June 12, 1993 presidential election mandate remains a defining moment in his political journey. Showunmi, in a statement titled “My Scar from MKO Abiola, My Sacrifice for Democracy, and My Unwavering Pan-Nigerian Conviction,” said the circumstances surrounding Abiola’s death and the annulment of the historic election had left an indelible mark on his life and political convictions. He also cautioned political actors against actions capable of undermining national stability, particularly the premature or unauthorised announcement of election results in ways that could trigger political tension and plunge the country into chaos. “The scar in my heart from the loss of Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola has not fully healed,” Showunmi said, adding that he would neither trivialise Abiola’s sacrifice nor pretend to be unfamiliar with the painful experiences that shaped Nigeria’s democratic struggle. He stressed that his remarks on the country’s political history had been misunderstood by some people, insisting that his intention was to caution against political conduct that could endanger peace, violate the law or destabilise the nation. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of the Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi has reaffirmed his commitment to Nigeria’s unity, democratic development and the ideals for which the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale (MKO) Abiola sacrificed his life, insisting that the struggle to actualise the June 12, 1993 presidential election mandate remains a defining moment in his political journey. Showunmi, in a statement titled “My Scar from MKO Abiola, My Sacrifice for Democracy, and My Unwavering Pan-Nigerian Conviction,” said the circumstances surrounding Abiola’s death and the annulment of the historic election had left an indelible mark on his life and political convictions. He also cautioned political actors against actions capable of undermining national stability, particularly the premature or unauthorised announcement of election results in ways that could trigger political tension and plunge the country into chaos. “The scar in my heart from the loss of Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola has not fully healed,” Showunmi said, adding that he would neither trivialise Abiola’s sacrifice nor pretend to be unfamiliar with the painful experiences that shaped Nigeria’s democratic struggle. He stressed that his remarks on the country’s political history had been misunderstood by some people, insisting that his intention was to caution against political conduct that could endanger peace, violate the law or destabilise the nation. Showunmi said his reference to the political events of 1992 was intended to illustrate the consequences of abandoning caution, restraint and respect for the law in the pursuit of political power. “I invoked the events of 1992 to illustrate how political situations can spiral out of control when caution, restraint and respect for the law are abandoned,” he said. He maintained that his intervention was intended as a warning about the potential consequences of political decisions, not an endorsement of reckless conduct. “My intervention was a warning about consequences, not an invitation to recklessness, and I will not permit reactionary forces to turn my counsel into something it was never intended to be,” he stated. According to him, political advice should be offered in the national interest, while individuals must ultimately decide whether to heed such counsel. He urged political contestants to consider the wider implications of their actions, warning that decisions taken without regard for the law and national stability could have far-reaching consequences for the country. Reaffirming his commitment to national unity, Showunmi declared that his political convictions were not driven by ethnic considerations and rejected any suggestion that he subscribed to the superiority of one ethnic group over another. “I must also state, unequivocally, that I am a Pan-Nigerian through and through. I have no interest in promoting the idea that one ethnic group is superior to another,” he said. He explained that his political philosophy was rooted in the collective dignity, security and prosperity of Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic or regional backgrounds. Showunmi urged Yoruba activists and others who might disagree with his position to consider his statements within the broader context of his commitment to Nigeria’s unity. “My words and actions must be understood within the framework of my commitment to the Nigerian nation. I will not subordinate that commitment to ethnic sentiment, sectional advantage or the politics of exclusion,” he said. He added that his preference for national cohesion should not be interpreted as a lack of personal conviction or an inadequate understanding of the country’s political history. On Nigeria’s political future, Showunmi reiterated his support for a power-sharing arrangement under which the presidency would rotate between the northern and southern parts of the country. He argued that a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation could help reduce political suspicion, strengthen national cohesion and promote democratic stability. “I have long expressed the view that Nigeria should manage political power through a pendulum arrangement between the Northern and Southern parts of the country,” he said. “In my considered opinion, a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation offers a framework for reducing suspicion, strengthening national cohesion and sustaining our democratic journey.” He described the proposal as part of the broader need for political maturity, mutual understanding and an inclusive approach to managing Nigeria’s diversity. Paying tribute to Abiola, the presumed winner of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, which was annulled by the military government, Showunmi said the late politician’s legacy remained inseparable from Nigeria’s struggle for democratic governance. He prayed that Abiola’s sacrifice would continue to inspire Nigerians to work towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. “May your supreme sacrifice continue to guide Nigeria towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. May the promise for which you paid such a terrible price never be betrayed,” he said. Showunmi also disclosed that he intended to speak more extensively in the future about his personal contributions to the pro-democracy struggle and how the events surrounding Abiola shaped his political trajectory. “One day, God willing, I will speak more fully about my own contributions to the struggle for democracy,” he said. According to him, the experiences surrounding Abiola and the struggle to reclaim the June 12 mandate influenced his political outlook and redirected the course of his life, setting in motion developments whose consequences he said were still unfolding. He also acknowledged the role played by media entrepreneur and publisher Dele Momodu during that period, describing his contribution as significant to that chapter of Nigeria’s political history. “I must also acknowledge Dele Momodu. May God spare his life. He played a key and pivotal role in that chapter of our history, and his contribution deserves to be remembered,” Showunmi said. Showunmi warned against interpreting his restraint as a lack of knowledge of Nigeria’s democratic history or mistaking his commitment to national unity for an absence of personal convictions. “Finally, let nobody mistake my restraint for ignorance of history or my commitment to national unity for an absence of personal conviction,” he said. He added: “My commitment is to Nigeria. My loyalty is to the democratic ideal. My respect for MKO Abiola’s sacrifice is enduring. And my conviction that Nigeria must survive, mature and prosper remains unshaken.” “May God bless Nigeria and all who genuinely labour for her progress,” he said. The post Showunmi reaffirms commitment to Abiola’s legacy, national unity appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps Call For Early Isolation Camp Preparations To Prevent Ebola Spread
item.description: The House of Representatives on Wednesday called for increased public awareness as well as early preparation of isolation camps following confirmation of a fresh outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). During a session on Wednesday, Reps members also called for alertness and asked the Federal Government to take advantage of the 2014 blueprint with which the Ebola virus was contained. The committee on infectious disease has been mandated to immediately swing into action to ensure that the resolutions of the House are promptly carried out. According to the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, the imported case of Ebola virus disease was confirmed by laboratory testing. Health workers attend a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) at Ongata Rongai, Kajiado County in Kenya on July 10, 2026. Speaking at a media briefing in Abuja, Pate said the patient is a woman with a recent travel history to East Africa, particularly Uganda, who returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7th, which progressed four days later before tests confirmed the infection. He said the patient is currently in isolation and receiving medical care, and contact tracing has commenced, with forty-four contacts already identified, as surveillance is strengthened at the country’s entry points. “The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital… where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed,” a government statement said. “She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care.” The Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate. Pate explained that the Ministry of Health, the FCT Health Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, and other partners are working together to contain the infection and prevent further spread. While urging public and private health facilities to remain on high alert, stressing that health workers must maintain a high index of suspicion for possible cases, he called on Nigerians to remain calm and vigilant. The minister advised the public to practise good hygiene, watch out for symptoms including fever, weakness, headache and diarrhoea, and cooperate with public health officials. He maintained that the situation is being managed, with the government pledging timely and transparent updates as efforts continue to contain the virus. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or with contaminated materials. Symptoms can include fever, headache, severe weakness, vomiting and diarrhoea. The post Reps Call For Early Isolation Camp Preparations To Prevent Ebola Spread appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: EU wants Booking.com to check out of its scam problem
item.description: The European Commission has opened an investigation under the Digital Services Act into whether Booking.com is doing enough to stop fraudsters running scams, phishing and smishing on its platform. Officials told The Register the probe, which opened Wednesday, covers a very large online platform (one with more than 45 million EU users) and has three strands. The first is whether Booking.com is failing to prevent fraudulent and non-compliant listings. "This is very much about people portraying themselves as the owner of premises and putting it up for rent while they are not the real owner," an EC spokesperson said. The second is whether it does enough to counter phishing and smishing (SMS phishing), and social engineering. "Scammers take over the account of a property owner and… portray themselves as the property owner, but also take over the contact details," she said. "So they start sending messages that people need to pay additional amounts." The Commission also suspects Booking.com is not sufficiently protecting the data of its consumers and business users. The third strand is advertising transparency: whether the platform clearly distinguishes ads from organic results, and whether it is clear about boosted listings, where property owners pay for higher ranking. Officials cited Booking.com's own admission in June 2024 of a 500-900 percent jump in travel scams over the previous 18 months. "What made us concerned is the very high figures," an official said. In the Netherlands alone, more than 1,000 fraud notifications were made in the first part of 2026, causing damage of €82,000, a tenfold increase on the previous year. “This is a real problem, and this is only the Dutch element,” the official said. “We have reports like that almost from all member states… So, we have clear elements where we find that the risk assessment was not sufficient, and as you know, the risk assessment is a key tool for us.” The Commission acknowledges that Booking.com assesses fraud using cases on its own platform and external reports, and takes internal measures in response. But “we feel that what they have done is absolutely substandard,” the official said. “Although they take measures, they could go much further, and they could have much more solid systems to prevent fraud.” “In the future we expect Booking.com to do a more diligent risk assessment,” she added. That could include addressing abuse of the reservation system, rapidly removing listings when fraud is reported, checking licenses, and changing how property owners are onboarded. A spokesperson at Booking.com told The Register : " We are cooperating fully with the European Commission and engaging constructively on its questions under the Digital Services Act (DSA). Security, trust and the protection of personal information are top priorities at Booking.com. We remain committed to working with relevant governments, regulators, law enforcement and industry partners to combat cybercrime and online fraud and prot

item.title: Hamzat mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti, says legacy will endure
item.description: The Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, has described the death of Pa Reuben Fasoranti, former National Leader of Afenifere, as a profound loss to the Yoruba race and Nigeria. Hamzat expressed his condolences in a message signed by Mr Tunde Alao, Senior Special Assistant to the Governor (Media), Office of the Deputy Governor, on Wednesday in Lagos. He extended his heartfelt sympathies, on behalf of his family, to the Fasoranti family, the government and people of Ondo State, and the entire Yoruba race over the death of the elder statesman at the age of 100. The deputy governor described Fasoranti as a distinguished educator, principled leader and respected voice in Nigeria’s socio-political landscape, whose life was devoted to justice, fairness and the preservation of Yoruba values within a united Nigeria. According to him, Fasoranti’s leadership of Afenifere reflected his unwavering commitment to the dignity, rights and aspirations of the Yoruba people. He said the late elder statesman’s courage, wisdom and steadfast adherence to principle earned him the respect of generations, making him a father figure, counsellor and custodian of enduring values in Yoruba leadership. “Pa Fasoranti lived a remarkable century of service to his people and humanity. His life was defined by integrity, conviction and an enduring commitment to justice. “He was a voice of wisdom whose counsel and principles will continue to inspire generations to come,” Hamzat said. The deputy governor noted that Fasoranti’s death was a significant loss not only to his immediate family and Ondo State but also to the Yoruba nation and Nigeria as a whole. He added that the late leader’s legacy of selfless service and principled leadership would remain a source of inspiration for generations to come. While acknowledging the grief occasioned by his death, the deputy governor urged the bereaved family and the Yoruba people to draw comfort from the enduring impact of Fasoranti’s life, the values he upheld and the many lives he touched. He prayed that Almighty God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give his family, loved ones and all those mourning his passing the strength and fortitude to bear the loss. (NAN) The post Hamzat mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti, says legacy will endure appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Football must not be detached from its roots as was the case with Manchester City | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Nasarawa vows to strengthen VAPP law implementation
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has reiterated its commitment to tackling gender-based violence through the implementation of the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Law, enacted in the state in January 2021. The Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Development, Rebecca Adamu Kwaji, gave the assurance on Wednesday at a two-day workshop on bridging gaps in the implementation of the VAPP Law through policy dialogue, capacity building, institutional compliance and accountability among duty-bearers. The workshop, held at Awa Diamond Hotel, Lafia, was organised with the support of CLEEN Foundation. Kwaji said the state government had demonstrated the political will to address gender-based violence by incorporating the VAPP Law into the state’s legal framework. She expressed optimism that stronger implementation of the law would help reduce cases of gender-based violence. “With this programme in place, I want to say it will bring about a reduction in gender-based violence,” she said. The commissioner said the ministry, through its Social Welfare Department, had been handling cases of gender-based violence, with alleged perpetrators prosecuted and survivors provided with care and support. She added that the ministry had established a shelter where survivors could receive assistance and remain safe until they recovered and could be separated from their abusers. Kwaji commended CLEEN Foundation for selecting Nasarawa as one of its focal states for efforts to strengthen stakeholders’ capacity to implement the law, improve public awareness and increase its visibility among residents. She expressed hope that the workshop would encourage stronger enforcement of the law and help stakeholders identify practical ways to address implementation challenges. “CLEEN Foundation has really come to take a very good position in our midst to help us put this law to be appreciated, because this Violence Against Persons law has been in place, but I don’t see it much executed, as not so much emphasis [has been] placed on it,” she said. “I believe that after this programme, this law will be very much recognised, and something new will be added to it,” she added. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has reiterated its commitment to tackling gender-based violence through the implementation of the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Law, enacted in the state in January 2021. The Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Development, Rebecca Adamu Kwaji, gave the assurance on Wednesday at a two-day workshop on bridging gaps in the implementation of the VAPP Law through policy dialogue, capacity building, institutional compliance and accountability among duty-bearers. The workshop, held at Awa Diamond Hotel, Lafia, was organised with the support of CLEEN Foundation. Kwaji said the state government had demonstrated the political will to address gender-based violence by incorporating the VAPP Law into the state’s legal framework. She expressed optimism that stronger implementation of the law would help reduce cases of gender-based violence. “With this programme in place, I want to say it will bring about a reduction in gender-based violence,” she said. The commissioner said the ministry, through its Social Welfare Department, had been handling cases of gender-based violence, with alleged perpetrators prosecuted and survivors provided with care and support. She added that the ministry had established a shelter where survivors could receive assistance and remain safe until they recovered and could be separated from their abusers. Kwaji commended CLEEN Foundation for selecting Nasarawa as one of its focal states for efforts to strengthen stakeholders’ capacity to implement the law, improve public awareness and increase its visibility among residents. She expressed hope that the workshop would encourage stronger enforcement of the law and help stakeholders identify practical ways to address implementation challenges. “CLEEN Foundation has really come to take a very good position in our midst to help us put this law to be appreciated, because this Violence Against Persons law has been in place, but I don’t see it much executed, as not so much emphasis [has been] placed on it,” she said. “I believe that after this programme, this law will be very much recognised, and something new will be added to it,” she added. Implementation gaps Earlier, the Executive Director of CLEEN Foundation, Peter Maduoma, said discussions on the VAPP Law centred on human rights, access to justice, public safety, institutional accountability and the protection of vulnerable persons. Maduoma, who was represented by the foundation’s Senior Programme Officer, Bernard Ekobay, acknowledged the support of the Royal Norwegian Embassy, saying its partnership had created opportunities for policy engagement, institutional strengthening and practical action towards more responsive and accountable justice and security institutions in Nigeria. He described the VAPP Law as an important legal framework for preventing violence, protecting survivors and holding perpetrators accountable. However, he said the existence of a law, regardless of how progressive its provisions might be, did not automatically guarantee justice for those who needed its protection. “The real test of the law is not simply whether it has been enacted, but whether a person experiencing domestic violence can safely seek help and receive a timely response; whether a survivor of sexual violence can report an incident without intimidation, stigma, or victim-blaming; whether a child exposed to abuse can access appropriate protection; and whether the institutions responsible for investigation, prosecution, adjudication, rehabilitation, and support can work together effectively,” he said. Maduoma identified limited public awareness of legal protections and reporting channels, poor coordination among relevant institutions, and weak or inconsistent investigation and prosecution as some of the challenges that could undermine implementation. He also listed inadequate survivor support services, resource and capacity constraints, and social pressures that discourage reporting or promote informal settlements in cases requiring legal accountability and survivor protection. He said stakeholders needed to establish the specific challenges affecting Nasarawa, identify weaknesses in institutional processes, assess existing successes and determine feasible reforms. “We need to understand which challenges are most pronounced in Nasarawa State, where institutional processes break down, what is already working, and which reforms are feasible within existing structures,” he said. He urged participants to engage constructively and work towards translating the law’s provisions into meaningful protection for residents. VAPP Law provides for compensation Also speaking, the Chairperson of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Nasarawa State chapter, Halima Hudu Abubakar, said the workshop could help improve the prosecution of offenders and strengthen the state’s response to gender-based violence. Abubakar said the Penal Code previously used in the state did not adequately address all forms of abuse, particularly physical, economic, sexual and emotional violence. She said the VAPP Law introduced provisions that could enable victims to seek compensation, in addition to the prosecution of offenders. “Before the coming of the VAPP Law, no law talked about compensating the victim. Only the offenders used to be prosecuted. Some of them don’t even know that they are supposed to go to court to seek for their rights,” she said. She argued that compensation could help victims obtain redress and reinforce accountability, while potentially discouraging repeat offences. Abubakar added that the full implementation of the law would help curb gender-based violence in Nasarawa State.
