item.title: Ebola: 5 things to know about Bundibugyo Strain as Nigeria confirms first case
item.description: Nigeria has confirmed its first case of Ebola virus disease caused by the Bundibugyo strain, prompting renewed attention to the symptoms, transmission, treatment and prevention of the infection. The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed on October 20, 2026, that the patient was a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda. She was receiving medical care in isolation in Abuja, while 44 contacts had been identified and were being monitored. Here are five things to know about the Bundibugyo Ebola strain. 1. Bundibugyo is a distinct Ebola virus species Bundibugyo strain is one of the viruses known to cause Ebola virus disease in humans. It was first identified during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda, in 2007. It is different from the Zaire ebolavirus species, which has caused several major Ebola outbreaks. The distinction matters because vaccines and treatments developed for one species may not protect against or treat another. 2. Symptoms include fever, weakness and diarrhoea Bundibugyo Ebola can cause symptoms that initially resemble those of other infections. Common symptoms include: Fever Severe weakness and fatigue Headache and muscle pain Abdominal pain Vomiting and diarrhoea In severe cases, patients may experience bleeding and complications affecting vital organs. However, bleeding does not occur in every case. Anyone experiencing compatible symptoms after possible exposure should seek prompt medical attention and tell healthcare workers about their travel history or contact with a suspected case. 3. The virus spreads through direct contact with infected bodily fluids Bundibugyo Ebola can spread through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of an infected person who is ill. Transmission can also occur through contaminated objects and contact with infected animals. The virus can enter the body through broken skin or the eyes, nose and mouth. Healthcare workers and family members caring for infected people may be at risk if appropriate infection-prevention measures are not followed. The incubation period for Ebola generally ranges from two to 21 days, meaning symptoms may take up to three weeks to appear after infection. 4. There is no licensed vaccine or specifically approved treatment for the strain According to the WHO, there are currently no licensed vaccines or specifically approved therapeutics for preventing or treating Bundibugyo virus disease. This differs from Ebola disease caused by the Zaire ebolavirus species, for which licensed vaccines and treatments are available. However, supportive medical care remains important. It may include intravenous fluids, correction of electrolyte imbalances, oxygen support, nutritional support and treatment of complications. The WHO has identified candidate vaccines and treatments for evaluation in clinical trials, including the remdesivir antiviral and experimental monoclonal antibodies. item.content:encoded: Nigeria has confirmed its first case of Ebola virus disease caused by the Bundibugyo strain, prompting renewed attention to the symptoms, transmission, treatment and prevention of the infection. The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed on October 20, 2026, that the patient was a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda. She was receiving medical care in isolation in Abuja, while 44 contacts had been identified and were being monitored. Here are five things to know about the Bundibugyo Ebola strain. 1. Bundibugyo is a distinct Ebola virus species Bundibugyo strain is one of the viruses known to cause Ebola virus disease in humans. It was first identified during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda, in 2007. It is different from the Zaire ebolavirus species, which has caused several major Ebola outbreaks. The distinction matters because vaccines and treatments developed for one species may not protect against or treat another. 2. Symptoms include fever, weakness and diarrhoea Bundibugyo Ebola can cause symptoms that initially resemble those of other infections. Common symptoms include: Fever Severe weakness and fatigue Headache and muscle pain Abdominal pain Vomiting and diarrhoea In severe cases, patients may experience bleeding and complications affecting vital organs. However, bleeding does not occur in every case. Anyone experiencing compatible symptoms after possible exposure should seek prompt medical attention and tell healthcare workers about their travel history or contact with a suspected case. 3. The virus spreads through direct contact with infected bodily fluids Bundibugyo Ebola can spread through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of an infected person who is ill. Transmission can also occur through contaminated objects and contact with infected animals. The virus can enter the body through broken skin or the eyes, nose and mouth. Healthcare workers and family members caring for infected people may be at risk if appropriate infection-prevention measures are not followed. The incubation period for Ebola generally ranges from two to 21 days, meaning symptoms may take up to three weeks to appear after infection. 4. There is no licensed vaccine or specifically approved treatment for the strain According to the WHO, there are currently no licensed vaccines or specifically approved therapeutics for preventing or treating Bundibugyo virus disease. This differs from Ebola disease caused by the Zaire ebolavirus species, for which licensed vaccines and treatments are available. However, supportive medical care remains important. It may include intravenous fluids, correction of electrolyte imbalances, oxygen support, nutritional support and treatment of complications. The WHO has identified candidate vaccines and treatments for evaluation in clinical trials, including the remdesivir antiviral and experimental monoclonal antibodies. These candidates should not be confused with established, specifically approved treatments for Bundibugyo Ebola. 5. Early detection and preventive measures are essential Preventing further transmission depends on identifying suspected cases quickly, isolating infected patients, tracing their contacts and monitoring exposed people for symptoms. Nigerians can reduce their risk by washing their hands regularly, avoiding contact with the blood and bodily fluids of suspected cases, and not handling sick or dead wild animals. Anyone who becomes unwell after possible exposure should seek medical attention promptly and provide accurate information about recent travel and contact with infected people. The NCDC and WHO remain key sources of official updates on the outbreak, case numbers and public health guidance. item.title: Flood submerges 18 Nasarawa communities, kills two
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has urged residents of flood-prone communities to heed warnings to relocate from low-lying areas to higher ground to avoid being swept away by recurring floods. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Nawani Aboki, made the appeal on Monday while briefing journalists on the recent flooding that submerged 18 communities in a development area of Doma Local Government Area of the state. Aboki said two people had died in the disaster, while several residents had been displaced and buildings and farmlands destroyed. He said Governor Abdullahi Sule had directed the Director-General of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency (NASEMA) to visit the affected communities to assess the extent of the damage and identify the necessary interventions. The commissioner said the government was expected to take concrete action following the assessment. “We are hoping that anytime this week, concrete actions will be taken by the government. Yesterday, when I was returning, I was there with the chairman of the local government to sympathise with the people and also condole with them,” he said. Describing the incident as massive flooding, Aboki expressed hope that the water would recede to allow residents to resume their normal activities. “It is not just normal flooding, but massive flooding that took place. We are hoping that the flooding will end and the waters will dry up so that people can resume their normal activities,” he said. He, however, warned residents against returning to their homes until the floodwaters had receded, citing concerns about the possibility of additional water flowing from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon. “But we have asked them not to go back yet. Let them wait until we see the water actually receding back to the River Benue again. We are not sure if more water will be coming in from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon. It will even be worse than it is currently,” he added. Aboki also reiterated the government’s commitment to providing support and relief supplies to the affected communities to prevent possible disease outbreaks. He explained that several smaller communities were clustered around larger settlements in the affected areas, increasing the pressure on host communities as displaced residents sought shelter. The commissioner cited Agyma, where more than eight communities were reportedly staying within the larger settlement, and Rukubi and Akpanaja, where several communities were also clustered. The government said it would continue to assess the situation and determine the necessary interventions as residents await the recession of the floodwaters. The post Flood submerges 18 Nasarawa communities, kills two appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: … Says 70% of healthcare spending comes from patients’ pockets … Only 10–13% of Nigerians covered by insurance … Seeks flexible premiums, prompt claims settlement By Chioma Obinna The HealthCare Providers Association of Nigeria (HCPAN), Lagos Branch, has called on the Federal and state governments to expand health insurance coverage, review tariffs paid to healthcare providers and ensure prompt settlement of claims, warning that low insurance penetration continues to expose millions of Nigerians to crippling medical expenses. The association said only about 10 to 13 per cent of Nigerians were covered by health insurance, while out-of-pocket payments accounted for approximately 70 per cent of healthcare expenditure, leaving many households financially vulnerable whenever illness occurs. HCPAN also called for flexible premium arrangements and community-based insurance schemes to bring market traders, artisans, transport workers, micro-entrepreneurs and other informal-sector workers into the health insurance system. The association made the call at its Scientific Conference and Annual General Meeting, AGM, held in Lagos, with the theme, “Expanding Health Insurance Coverage in Nigeria: Improving Community-Based Insurance Schemes in the Informal Sector.” Speaking at the event, the Chairman of HCPAN Lagos Branch, Pharmacist Biola Paul-Ozieh, said the country’s high dependence on direct payments for healthcare remained a major obstacle to achieving universal health coverage, despite the mandatory health insurance provisions of the National Health Insurance Authority, NHIA, Act, 2022. “Currently, it is reported that about 10 to 13 per cent of the Nigerian population is covered by health insurance. The out-of-pocket expenditure is still huge at roughly 70 per cent despite the mandatory clause in the NHIA Act 2022,” she said. Paul-Ozieh added that coverage of vulnerable groups stood at about 3.8 million, while participation among informal-sector workers remained limited, with enrolment concentrated mainly in Lagos and Abuja. item.dc:creator: Urowayino Jeremiah
item.content:encoded: … Says 70% of healthcare spending comes from patients’ pockets … Only 10–13% of Nigerians covered by insurance … Seeks flexible premiums, prompt claims settlement By Chioma Obinna The HealthCare Providers Association of Nigeria (HCPAN), Lagos Branch, has called on the Federal and state governments to expand health insurance coverage, review tariffs paid to healthcare providers and ensure prompt settlement of claims, warning that low insurance penetration continues to expose millions of Nigerians to crippling medical expenses. The association said only about 10 to 13 per cent of Nigerians were covered by health insurance, while out-of-pocket payments accounted for approximately 70 per cent of healthcare expenditure, leaving many households financially vulnerable whenever illness occurs. HCPAN also called for flexible premium arrangements and community-based insurance schemes to bring market traders, artisans, transport workers, micro-entrepreneurs and other informal-sector workers into the health insurance system. The association made the call at its Scientific Conference and Annual General Meeting, AGM, held in Lagos, with the theme, “Expanding Health Insurance Coverage in Nigeria: Improving Community-Based Insurance Schemes in the Informal Sector.” Speaking at the event, the Chairman of HCPAN Lagos Branch, Pharmacist Biola Paul-Ozieh, said the country’s high dependence on direct payments for healthcare remained a major obstacle to achieving universal health coverage, despite the mandatory health insurance provisions of the National Health Insurance Authority, NHIA, Act, 2022. “Currently, it is reported that about 10 to 13 per cent of the Nigerian population is covered by health insurance. The out-of-pocket expenditure is still huge at roughly 70 per cent despite the mandatory clause in the NHIA Act 2022,” she said. Paul-Ozieh added that coverage of vulnerable groups stood at about 3.8 million, while participation among informal-sector workers remained limited, with enrolment concentrated mainly in Lagos and Abuja. She identified delayed claims payments, tariffs that failed to reflect prevailing economic realities, negative attitudes among some enrollees and the exclusion of certain healthcare professionals from insurance programmes as challenges undermining providers’ participation. “The other concern we have as providers is the various challenges faced by varied professionals in not being included in the provision of health services in the health insurance programme,” she said. The HCPAN chairman said sustainable community-based insurance schemes would require stronger collaboration between government and private healthcare providers, alongside policies that addressed the financial realities of informal-sector workers. Informal sector holds key to wider coverage The Chief Executive Officer of DrugStoc Limited, Dr Chibuzo Opara, who delivered the keynote address through his representative, Dr Damilare Ojo, said expanding enrolment alone would not guarantee universal health coverage unless insurance schemes enabled beneficiaries to obtain the treatment and medicines they needed. “What does it mean to have health insurance if, when illness occurs, the person cannot access the care needed?” he asked. Opara said insurance coverage remained concentrated in the formal sector, leaving traders, artisans, transport workers and small-business owners inadequately protected against healthcare costs. He explained that irregular incomes made fixed insurance contributions difficult for many informal-sector workers, stressing that schemes must be designed around their economic circumstances. “We cannot close this gap by simply increasing enrolment in existing schemes. If we genuinely want to achieve universal health coverage, we must develop insurance models that address the needs of the people we intend to cover,” he said. He advocated flexible contributions, appropriate benefit packages and group enrolment through trusted associations to encourage participation. Opara also called for community pharmacies to be integrated into insurance networks, describing them as accessible points where residents could obtain initial healthcare advice and medicines. He urged stakeholders to assess the effectiveness of insurance schemes through measurable outcomes, including access to medicines, service utilisation, referral outcomes, claims processing times, policy renewals and reductions in out-of-pocket expenditure. Lagos expands grassroots enrolment Meanwhile, the Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to expanding health insurance through affordable premiums, grassroots enrolment and the integration of community pharmacies and diagnostic centres into the healthcare network. The state Commissioner for Health, Professor Akin Abayomi, represented by the Deputy Director of the Research Unit at the Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr Tolu Babatope, said the informal sector accounted for a significant proportion of Lagos residents who often struggled to pay for medical treatment. He said the Lagos State Health Management Agency, LASHMA, was expanding affordable premium options and grassroots enrolment initiatives in line with the state’s policy on mandatory health insurance. Abayomi described community pharmacies as important entry points into the healthcare system, noting that their integration into insurance schemes could bring services closer to residents and strengthen access to treatment. “Community pharmacies, therefore, are no longer merely places where medicines are dispensed. They can serve as important points of contact for healthcare services and entry points into the health insurance network,” he said. He disclosed that the state was also working to strengthen links between pharmacies, hospitals and diagnostic centres, while addressing concerns about tariffs, delayed claims payments and inadequate digital infrastructure. Delivering the sub-theme, the Lagos Zonal Coordinator of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), Pharmacist Femi Adeoye, who was represented by the State Coordinator, NHIA, Yaba Office, Pharmacist Chinenye Nwaohiri, highlighted opportunities for different healthcare professionals to participate in expanding health insurance. Adeoye said the NHIA operated programmes covering formal-sector workers, informal groups, private-sector participants and state health insurance schemes, with health maintenance organisations also supporting service delivery. He explained that initiatives such as the Basic Health Care Provision Fund and the Vulnerable Group Fund were designed to improve access to healthcare for people who might otherwise struggle to afford treatment. He called for fair tariff reviews that reflected the cost of providing services and urged healthcare professionals to take advantage of opportunities within the insurance system. “Fair tariff reviews and timely payment for services are essential to encouraging healthcare providers to participate in health insurance schemes and ensuring sustainable service delivery.” He stressed that public confidence depended on enrollees receiving timely and appropriate care, adding that reliable service delivery was essential to sustaining participation in insurance schemes. In his goodwill message, the National President of HCPAN, Dr Austin Aipoh, called for stronger collaboration among stakeholders and flexible payment arrangements to make health insurance more accessible to informal-sector workers. Aipoh said community-based approaches could help reach people whose incomes were irregular and who might not be able to afford conventional insurance contributions. He also urged policymakers to create an enabling environment for healthcare providers, stressing that insurance schemes must be structured to support both patients and the professionals responsible for delivering care. item.title: Java crashes the departure board at Tyne and Wear Metro
item.description: Java has elbowed its way onto a Tyne and Wear Metro information display, giving passengers an error message alongside their train times. Eagle-eyed Register reader abend0c4 spotted the sign, whose dialog design suggests a rather elderly Windows installation. Could it be Windows 7 in Classic guise, or perhaps Windows Server 2008 R2? Both wheezed their last in 2023, when the Extended Security Updates (ESU) program ended. Or perhaps POSReady 7? That kept going (again via ESU) until October 8, 2024 . Not that the end of ESU means the code will suddenly stop working. Just that Microsoft has called a halt to updates. The Tyne and Wear Metro is no stranger to keeping old technology running past its expiration date. Opened in August 1980 , the transit network has been replacing its aging rolling stock with new units, but the signage has endured. Then again, compared to the Commodore VIC-20 and Apple II, which ruled the home computing roost in 1980, perhaps an operating system that's only been obsolete for a few years isn't such a bad thing. Any second now somebody will be writing an email about some hardware by Sinclair, Acorn, or their particular device maker of choice. But back to the sign. Sadly, it's unclear which version of Java has elbowed its way to the foreground. Java's troubleshooting guidance lists video driver problems as one possible cause of this error. The train indicator seems to be operating as normal if somewhat obscured by Java's attempt to be the centre of attention," our reader noted. Java is longer be a bright young thing, yet it still keeps plenty of enterprise systems running behind the scenes. On this occasion, it appears to prefer the foreground. We'd prefer it kept a lower profile. Passengers have enough ups and downs without Java throwing its toys out of the virtual pram. ®

item.title: AFENIFERE RIFT: Those still making noise in cuckoo land – Omololu
item.description: By Dickson Omobola National Organising Secretary of Afenifere, Abagun Omololu, has expressed optimism about the future of the pan-Yoruba socio-cultural organisation after the death of its leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, saying those still making noise on the sidelines are crying in a cloud of cuckoo land. Recall that in the build-up to the 2023 general elections, which brought President Bola Tinubu to power, acting leader of Afenifere, the late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, supported Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, while the substantive leader, Fasoranti, supported Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, causing a division within the organisation. Speaking on The Morning Show, an Arise TV programme, Wednesday, Omololu described the period as unfortunate, saying such a development had never occurred in Yorubaland. He said: “It is an unfortunate period that we had before the 2023 election that got the acting leader and the substantive leader backing separate candidates. It’s an unfortunate thing. It had never happened in the history of Yorubaland.” On the future of Afenifere, he said: “The future of Afenifere is fantastic. Somebody came to be appointed a leader. The era of Baba Adebanjo is gone. Whoever that is still making noise on the side, I see it as a cry in a cloud of cuckoo land.” On Fasoranti’s legacy, he said: “To those of us who are very close to Baba, we have lost something in humanity. An embodiment of contentment, of somebody who sees public service as a sacrifice. Baba graduated from the University of Ibadan in 1951. There were not many graduates then. Immediately, he became a part of the Action Group of the late Obafemi Awolowo. He was a young man of 25 years old. Not many of his contemporaries were graduates. “Baba (Awolowo) pulled him, he worked with the likes of Professor Aluko, Professor Aboyade Cole and the rest. These are phenomenal leaders who came to the world for service. That is what Baba is for us. There was a time Baba lost his wife. Now he used to be made the governor of Ondo State, which a lot of people are dying for. They are using drug money, they are using everything now to buy the position. “The position was presented on the platter of gold to Baba, but he said, no, I cannot be a governor without having a wife, and I’m not ready to marry again. What a human being. Baba refused the position. That is why the position went to Baba Adefarati. This is a kind of human being. Baba’s life was Awoism. It’s not something where you march to gain political attention. It’s an inborn thing in him. We are going to serve the less privileged. That is what Baba is all about and Awoism. Egalitarian society. Let the rich get richer, while the poor must be looked after. These fingers are not equal. That is why they call us welfarists. That’s what Baba stood for. All his life. That was what Awolowo handed over to us.” The post AFENIFERE RIFT: Those still making noise in cuckoo land – Omololu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PSG’s Kvaratskhelia Set For Long Absence With Torn ACL
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia requires surgery after tearing his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona, the European champions, said on Wednesday. “Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” PSG said in a statement. PSG’s Georgian forward Khvicha Kvaratskhelia lies on the pitch after sustaining an injury during the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 20, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) In more bad news for PSG, the club said forward Ousmane Dembele and central defender Marquinhos will both be sidelined for “several weeks” with injuries. Kvaratskhelia slumped to the turf without any apparent contact and left the pitch just before the hour mark in the 4-2 league phase victory against Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday. The 25-year-old Georgia international played a leading role in helping PSG to win back-to-back Champions League titles and is one of the contenders for the Ballon d’Or, which will be awarded on Monday. Dembele, the current Ballon d’Or holder, and Marquinhos both suffered thigh injuries, PSG said. Vitinha’s superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season’s Champions League. The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year’s Ballon d’Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes. Fabian Ruiz then sealed PSG’s third victory in as many outings in this season’s competition, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third season running. AFP The post PSG’s Kvaratskhelia Set For Long Absence With Torn ACL appeared first on Channels Television .

item.description: PRP candidate blames poverty, unemployment for kidnapping, banditry The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has described Nigeria as a failed state, citing worsening poverty, unemployment, insecurity and economic decline. Duke said he decided to contest the 2027 presidential election because he could no longer remain on the sidelines while the country’s challenges deepened without offering himself as an alternative. Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, the former Cross River State governor said he was driven by what he described as the urgency of rescuing Nigeria from its current trajectory. “You get to a point in your life where you say, ‘Either I walk away or I do something.’ “There is no guarantee that you will win. But I don’t want to look back and say that all these things happened and I did nothing,” he said. Duke said Nigeria could not afford another four years of what he described as its present economic and social decline. “I talk about the urgency of now because I don’t think we can go on like this for another four years,” he said. He added that his campaign would focus on policy options and solutions to the country’s challenges rather than personalities. “What I want to do is focus on those who aspire to lead this nation on addressing the issues that affect us and how we can resolve them. “I talk about the options. I talk about the real issues. I don’t want to talk about personalities,” he said. On insecurity, Duke argued that Nigeria’s security challenges could not be separated from the economy’s failure to create enough opportunities for its growing population. “If we don’t address these issues squarely and fundamentally, we’re already a failed state. There’s no question about it. “Look at what is happening — banditry, terrorism, kidnapping and all sorts of conflicts. These are symptoms of a state that is unable, not only to properly articulate its challenges, but to deal with them,” he said. Explaining his assessment, Duke said the existence of a government and public institutions did not necessarily mean that a state was meeting its responsibilities to citizens. “What is the definition of a failed state? item.content:encoded: PRP candidate blames poverty, unemployment for kidnapping, banditry The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has described Nigeria as a failed state, citing worsening poverty, unemployment, insecurity and economic decline. Duke said he decided to contest the 2027 presidential election because he could no longer remain on the sidelines while the country’s challenges deepened without offering himself as an alternative. Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, the former Cross River State governor said he was driven by what he described as the urgency of rescuing Nigeria from its current trajectory. “You get to a point in your life where you say, ‘Either I walk away or I do something.’ “There is no guarantee that you will win. But I don’t want to look back and say that all these things happened and I did nothing,” he said. Duke said Nigeria could not afford another four years of what he described as its present economic and social decline. “I talk about the urgency of now because I don’t think we can go on like this for another four years,” he said. He added that his campaign would focus on policy options and solutions to the country’s challenges rather than personalities. “What I want to do is focus on those who aspire to lead this nation on addressing the issues that affect us and how we can resolve them. “I talk about the options. I talk about the real issues. I don’t want to talk about personalities,” he said. On insecurity, Duke argued that Nigeria’s security challenges could not be separated from the economy’s failure to create enough opportunities for its growing population. “If we don’t address these issues squarely and fundamentally, we’re already a failed state. There’s no question about it. “Look at what is happening — banditry, terrorism, kidnapping and all sorts of conflicts. These are symptoms of a state that is unable, not only to properly articulate its challenges, but to deal with them,” he said. Explaining his assessment, Duke said the existence of a government and public institutions did not necessarily mean that a state was meeting its responsibilities to citizens. “What is the definition of a failed state? Fundamentally, it is a state that fails to meet the aspirations of its people. “You may still have a government and institutions, but if the state cannot protect the people and provide the environment in which they can live productive lives, then it is failing them,” he said. He added that victims of kidnapping would have little reason to be concerned about academic debates over the definition of a failed state when they had experienced the consequences of insecurity. “Talk to someone who has been kidnapped. That person does not need you to explain the definition of a failed state. His experience has already told him what failure of the state means,” he said. Middle class disappearing Duke also lamented what he described as the virtual disappearance of Nigeria’s middle class, arguing that economic pressures had left many households struggling to meet their daily needs. “You have perhaps one per cent who are genuinely wealthy and then a huge number of people struggling around or below the poverty line. “The so-called middle class does not really exist anymore. Many of those we call middle class are only surviving from day-to-day. Let there be one serious emergency and they crumble,” he said. He said businesses were contracting while new enterprises were not emerging fast enough to absorb the growing number of people entering the labour market. “Businesses are contracting. New ones are not springing up the way they should. At the same time, we are turning out graduates every year and adding more people to the working population, but there is no work for them to do,” he said. The PRP candidate also linked poverty and unemployment to kidnapping and banditry, arguing that efforts to tackle insecurity would remain inadequate without addressing the underlying economic conditions. “When it comes to banditry and kidnapping, poverty and unemployment are at the bottom of much of it. “We keep reacting to these crises instead of asking what is producing them. We are too reactive in our governance. Governance is not just about today; it is about laying the foundation for tomorrow,” he said. Oil output, population growth Duke said another issue the presidential campaign should address was whether Nigeria’s economy had expanded sufficiently to support its growing population. Comparing the country’s crude oil production with its population growth, he said Nigeria’s economic capacity had not kept pace with the number of people it needed to support. “In 1980, Nigeria was producing about 2.5 million barrels of oil a day. Forty-six years later, we are producing around 1.7 million barrels, while our population has tripled. “So you have to ask: has the economy expanded enough to carry the population? Clearly, it has not,” he said. He argued that Nigeria’s population should be an economic asset if citizens had access to quality education, employment and opportunities to contribute productively to the economy. “Our numbers ought to be an asset. But a large population is an asset only when you can educate the people, employ them and make them productive,” he said. Duke warned that continued economic hardship could encourage more Nigerians with the means to emigrate, while those remaining in the country faced mounting pressure. Why I returned to Nigeria The presidential candidate said his ambition was also rooted in his decision decades ago to return to Nigeria after studying and working in the United States. “I had the opportunity in my twenties to remain in America. I went to school there and worked there for a while. “But I voluntarily decided that was not where I wanted to be. I believe the Almighty put me in Nigeria for a reason. I believe in this country’s possibilities, and this is where I believe I should contribute,” he said. Duke said the same conviction informed his decision to contest the Cross River governorship election in 1999 and had now motivated him to seek the country’s highest political office. “I wanted to prove then that we were better than what we were putting forward. From experience, I know Nigeria can be a very successful nation,” he said. The post Nigeria already a failed state, middle class gone — Duke appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Elon Musk ordered reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine – Report
item.description: Elon Musk ordered a reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday, after the tech billionaire said any limits on the SpaceX-operated communications system would ultimately have come from the president. Musk capped the speed at which Ukrainian equipment could connect to the system, making some of Kyiv’s drones useless, the Journal reported, citing anonymous US officials and people familiar with the matter. Kyiv has accused Washington of deliberately slowing speeds at which Starshield can be used effectively — a charge denied last week by US President Donald Trump. Musk had previously said that “any limits on speed or usage” of Starshield systems were “decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” referring to Trump. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Washington had no prior knowledge of the slowdown. “The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr. Musk,” Rubio said during his trip to India. “That’s a private company; the president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything… I’m telling you, there was no foreknowledge.” On Tuesday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said that the Pentagon had not directed any changes to Starshield, saying: “We haven’t pulled anything back.” “Nothing’s changed from our view. We haven’t made any directives or anything like that,” he said. Trump said last week he did not request any curbs to Starshield, adding: “It wasn’t me. And I don’t think it was Elon.” Kyiv last week reported restrictions to the service, which it sees as crucial to fending off Moscow’s invasion, shortly after Trump criticized Ukraine and urged it to stop targeting Russian oil refineries. Ukraine uses Starshield, Starlink’s military-grade satellite service, for its battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russia-occupied territory, and its interceptor drones. It also uses SpaceX’s parallel Starlink civilian satellite system. Relations between Washington and Kyiv have been increasingly tense in recent days, with Trump calling for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to be replaced after he criticized a US deal allowing more Russian diesel into global markets. AFP The post Elon Musk ordered reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine – Report appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mimiko mourns Uduaghan, hails him as detribalised statesman
item.description: Ex-Delta governor was bridge-builder across party lines By Dayo Johnson, Akure Former Ondo State Governor, Dr. Olusegun Mimiko, has mourned the death of former Delta State Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, describing him as a detribalised statesman who left indelible footprints in Delta State and Nigeria. Mimiko, in a statement he personally signed, said he and his wife, Olukemi, received the news of Uduaghan’s death with sadness. Uduaghan reportedly died in the early hours of Monday, October 19, 2026, after an illness. “We mourn the departure of Dr. Uduaghan, a complete gentleman, a medical doctor who brought compassion into governance, and a detribalised statesman who left indelible footprints across Delta State and Nigeria,” Mimiko said. He noted that Uduaghan served Delta State in various capacities, including Commissioner for Health, Secretary to the State Government and governor, discharging his responsibilities with grace, humility and calmness, even in times of crisis. Describing the late former governor as a bridge-builder, Mimiko said he maintained cordial relationships across political divides. “He was a bridge-builder and a brother across party lines,” he said. Mimiko extended his condolences to Uduaghan’s wife, Roli, his children, the Uduaghan family of Abigborodo, the Delta State Government and the people of the state, as well as others mourning his death. He noted that the loss was particularly painful as it came just days before Uduaghan’s 72nd birthday. “We pray Almighty God grants his soul eternal rest and grants his family the fortitude to bear this irreplaceable loss. “May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace,” Mimiko added. The post Mimiko mourns Uduaghan, hails him as detribalised statesman appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Calvin’s Mom and Dad, who have no names beyond that, each have their own individual dynamic with Calvin. As for Calvin’s Dad , while Calvin drives him bonkers too, there’s another dynamic where the dad will sometimes tell Calvin ridiculous things just to see if his son will believe them, which he often does.

item.title: The spec is the new code, so brush up on your prose, says Kaseya CTO
item.description: Software developers will need to get their kicks from becoming code coaches of AI, professors of prompt engineering, and masters of their domain. So says Pratik Wadher, chief technology officer at Kaseya, who oversaw a team of codesmiths rewriting software across the company’s managed services portfolio, which spans remote monitoring and management, backup and recovery, cybersecurity, and automation. “The goal is unifying our data, unifying our API, but as we are starting to also look at the product portfolio that we have, we're trying to understand what are the patterns that we can use to consolidate the product workflows,” he tells The Register . Storage is a good example. The basic workflows involve reading and writing data to storage arrays, Kaseya's own cloud environment, or the racks run by hyperscalers. The team re-architected the back end of its storage products so the storage engine reads and writes to any kind of storage from ZFS to S3. “This is where AI helps,” Wadher claims. “Fundamentally we have accelerated that piece of re-architecture.” Since joining Kaseya in September 2025, the CTO has been trying to simplify what he admits can be a “confusing” number of individual products. “The storage layer that we've been writing, we re-architected and wrote it in six weeks. And that's the actual writing, implementing and testing the code. There are years of domain expertise behind understanding how we want to write it.” In the process, Kaseya used Anthropic coding agents to help a human write the spec. The meatbags at Kaseya then iterated on it and peer-reviewed it with critique agents, before the AI generated the code. Anthropic’s Claude is becoming the “de facto standard” for writing code at Kaseya . “ When I look at my engineers, it's not how I used to write code. It's almost like I'm manipulating these agents, but the best engineers are still critical, because you have developed a lot of experience in understanding what you need to do,” Wadher says. Does this take the fun out of coding? Yes and no, he claims. Mirroring the wider industry, some Kaseya engineers are embracing the new approach and some are more “hesitant.” “ The fun part of coding is going to be the design, the architecture, the thinking. Writing code is fun but I don't think it's [ the ] fun [part]. The fun part is having the code run, seeing what it can do, and then tweaking it and changing it. If you can accelerate that and start seeing the results, I think that, for me at least, that would be the fun part: seeing the impact.” Developers must become proficient prompters and “you need the domain expertise,” he adds. “If you’re just using AI to generate code I don’t think you’re going to be useful and I don't think the code you're writing is going to be useful.” Some Reg readers and some of the article-writing vultures may disagree. If you can accelerate that and start seeing the results, I think that, for me at least, that would be the fun part: seeing the impact.” Developers must become proficient prompters and “you need the domain expertise,” he adds. “If you’re just using AI to generate code I don’t think you’re going to be useful and I don't think the code you're writing is going to be useful.” Some Reg readers and some of the article-writing vultures may disagree. There is a clear split happening in the world of FOSS, for example, where some projects want only human-written code and others take what they describe as a more pragmatic view of AI tools . AI is already forcing change upon the tech sector. Research last year suggested the number of graduates starting a career in technology is plunging with certain functions being subsumed by agents. “I think basic tasks will be done by AI, so you're not going to need that,” Wadher says. “The skills that will be extremely important are critical thinking and writing. “The worst part of coding, [the thing] engineers hate is writing the documentation. Well, guess what? That is going to become even more critical now. Being able to write clear, concise design specifications, the functional specifications, is going to be extremely important. The good thing is that you’ll now have an [AI] partner that can do this with you and you can iterate with this partner. “I would say the new code is the spec. That's what you're going to check into GitHub now, because you want to make sure that the spec you wrote is going to generate the same type of code now over and over again. I have seen variances." ®

item.title: Russian satellite plays 'cat-and-mouse' with a commercial US spacecraft likely used by Ukraine. But why the risky close encounter?
item.description: null A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit. A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it? 1/2New blogpost:"KOSMOS 2612 and ICEYE-X36: a worrisome cat-and-mouse-game in Space"(link to blogpost in next tweet) https://t.co/bzNtADpIrA October 17, 2026 Not an isolated incident A worrisome cat-and-mouse-game in Space Dr, Marco Langbroek, satellite tracker Before tackling that question, we need to set the stage a bit. For example, it's important to note that inspections aren't unheard of in the final frontier. Russia , the United States and China have all maneuvered satellites into close proximity of other nations' hardware in recent years. Most of this activity has taken place in geostationary orbit , which lies 22,236 miles (35,786 kilometers) above Earth. At this altitude, orbital velocity matches our planet's rotational speed, allowing spacecraft to "hover" over one patch of Earth continuously. GEO is therefore a popular destination for spy, communications and weather satellites — and for spacecraft designed to shadow and assess them. Kosmos 2612 is operating in low Earth orbit (LEO), which is part of the reason its activities have created such a stir. Neither China nor the U.S. has conducted an uncooperative rendezvous in LEO, as far as we know. But Russia has, according to Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability for the nonprofit Secure World Foundation. "They've done a few," she told Space.com. "Kosmos 2543 got within about 30 kilometers [19 miles] of USA 245 in January 2020, and then Kosmos 2558 got within about 70 kilometers [43 miles] of USA 326 in August 2022. And they've done repeated approaches to 326." Kosmos 2612 got much closer to its target than those other inspectors did, of course. And there's another big difference: USA 245 and USA 326 are classified spy satellites managed by the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, while ICEYE-X36 is a private Earth-observing craft . item.content:encoded: null A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit. A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it? 1/2New blogpost:"KOSMOS 2612 and ICEYE-X36: a worrisome cat-and-mouse-game in Space"(link to blogpost in next tweet) https://t.co/bzNtADpIrA October 17, 2026 Not an isolated incident A worrisome cat-and-mouse-game in Space Dr, Marco Langbroek, satellite tracker Before tackling that question, we need to set the stage a bit. For example, it's important to note that inspections aren't unheard of in the final frontier. Russia , the United States and China have all maneuvered satellites into close proximity of other nations' hardware in recent years. Most of this activity has taken place in geostationary orbit , which lies 22,236 miles (35,786 kilometers) above Earth. At this altitude, orbital velocity matches our planet's rotational speed, allowing spacecraft to "hover" over one patch of Earth continuously. GEO is therefore a popular destination for spy, communications and weather satellites — and for spacecraft designed to shadow and assess them. Kosmos 2612 is operating in low Earth orbit (LEO), which is part of the reason its activities have created such a stir. Neither China nor the U.S. has conducted an uncooperative rendezvous in LEO, as far as we know. But Russia has, according to Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability for the nonprofit Secure World Foundation. "They've done a few," she told Space.com. "Kosmos 2543 got within about 30 kilometers [19 miles] of USA 245 in January 2020, and then Kosmos 2558 got within about 70 kilometers [43 miles] of USA 326 in August 2022. And they've done repeated approaches to 326." Kosmos 2612 got much closer to its target than those other inspectors did, of course. And there's another big difference: USA 245 and USA 326 are classified spy satellites managed by the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, while ICEYE-X36 is a private Earth-observing craft . Russia's Luch-2 satellite approaches another geostationary satellite on April 12, 2024, as tracked by the French company Aldoria's observation stations. (Image credit: Aldoria) Eyes in the sky There are about 80 ICEYE spacecraft in LEO at the moment. They image our planet using SAR, which can peer through clouds and gather data both day and night. Some of these satellites are operated by ICEYE, a company based in Finland, while others are managed by its American subsidiary, ICEYE US. ICEYE-X36 is one of the latter. At least some ICEYE satellites provide imagery to Ukraine , which Russia invaded in February 2022 and continues to assault with ground troops and missile and drone attacks. Indeed, ICEYE signed a contract this past January firming up this data-sharing relationship with Ukraine. "The agreement ensures that the Ministry of Defence continues to receive a high volume of high-resolution satellite imagery through ICEYE's world-leading SAR constellation, supporting the Ukrainian Armed Forces with persistent situational awareness on tactical timelines," ICEYE representatives said in a January statement . That likely explains Russia's interest in ICEYE satellites, which is extensive and longstanding. For example, Kosmos 2612 launched in April of this year with five other spacecraft. In May, four members of this fleet, including Kosmos 2612, conducted maneuvers to get into a co-planar orbit with ICEYE-X36 . Such maneuvers use a lot of fuel and are therefore not performed lightly. (It's unclear if ICEYE-X36 is dedicated to capturing imagery of Ukraine or Russia, but Russia certainly seems to think it is.) However, we still don't know the purpose of Kosmos 2612's close approach ( which is apparently over , at least for now), Samson stressed. There are a few possibilities. For example, Russia may want to get a better idea of ICEYE satellites' capabilities, and/or figure out what exactly they're studying on Earth below. Or maybe Kosmos 2612 was actively interfering with ICEYE-X36 in some way — messing with its sensors, perhaps, or blocking or intercepting its communications with the ground. However, Samson leans toward another explanation. "I think they're getting frustrated," she said of the Russians. "They've been kind of in a stalemate, particularly for the past six months or so. And so I think it's just more a matter of demonstrating military prowess in a manner that the Ukrainians cannot respond to," she added. "The Ukrainians are just as good, perhaps even better than, the Russians on drones. But when it comes to space stuff, they're not peers, and this is just a way to remind everyone that that's the case." As Kosmos 2612's activities show, space is becoming an increasingly competitive and contested domain. The U.S. has long held the advantage above Earth, fielding the most capable reconnaissance and communications craft, but Russia and China are challenging that dominance . This drama is unfolding above our heads now, and it affects everyone on the planet. Samson therefore wishes that governments around the world were more forthcoming about their space activities — for example, that we learned about Kosmos 2612's shenanigans from the U.S .Space Force rather than from private companies and civilians who pore over government tracking data. "I think it just speaks to the importance of transparency, and sharing information about these sort of things," she said. "As much as you may want to, you cannot keep the existence of satellites classified, because people can see them."

item.title: Uganda Debunks Claims Of Ebola Outbreak After Nigeria Confirmed Infection
item.description: Uganda’s Ministry of Health has denied reports of an Ebola outbreak in the country following confirmation of a case in Nigeria. The Federal Government had on Tuesday confirmed a case of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Nigeria’s confirmed case comes amid an ongoing Ebola outbreak linked to the Bundibugyo virus in the DRC, with infections also reported in other countries. According to the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, the imported case of Ebola virus disease was confirmed by laboratory testing. Speaking at a media briefing in Abuja, Pate said the patient is a woman with a recent travel history to East Africa, particularly Uganda, who returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7th, which progressed four days later before tests confirmed the infection. He said the patient is currently in isolation and receiving medical care, and contact tracing has commenced, with forty-four contacts already identified, as surveillance is strengthened at the country’s entry points. “The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital… where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed,” a government statement said. “She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care.” Pate explained that the Ministry of Health, the FCT Health Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, and other partners are working together to contain the infection and prevent further spread. Nigeria’s health minister Ali Pate. While urging public and private health facilities to remain on high alert, stressing that health workers must maintain a high index of suspicion for possible cases, he called on Nigerians to remain calm and vigilant. The minister advised the public to practise good hygiene, watch out for symptoms including fever, weakness, headache and diarrhoea, and cooperate with public health officials. He maintained that the situation is being managed, with the government pledging timely and transparent updates as efforts continue to contain the virus. The health minister said the government is drawing on Nigeria’s experience in containing the 2014 Ebola outbreak and the public health mechanisms established over the years, adding that all identified contacts are being traced and monitored. A health worker prepares to administer a vaccine developed for a strain of the Ebola virus at the Provincial Laboratory of Ituri in the northeastern province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, on September 19, 2026. Reacting to the report, however, in a public statement issued on Tuesday, the Ugandan ministry said “The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said, adding that travel through Uganda alone was insufficient to establish where the infection occurred. item.content:encoded: Uganda’s Ministry of Health has denied reports of an Ebola outbreak in the country following confirmation of a case in Nigeria. The Federal Government had on Tuesday confirmed a case of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Nigeria’s confirmed case comes amid an ongoing Ebola outbreak linked to the Bundibugyo virus in the DRC, with infections also reported in other countries. According to the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, the imported case of Ebola virus disease was confirmed by laboratory testing. Speaking at a media briefing in Abuja, Pate said the patient is a woman with a recent travel history to East Africa, particularly Uganda, who returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7th, which progressed four days later before tests confirmed the infection. He said the patient is currently in isolation and receiving medical care, and contact tracing has commenced, with forty-four contacts already identified, as surveillance is strengthened at the country’s entry points. “The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital… where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed,” a government statement said. “She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care.” Pate explained that the Ministry of Health, the FCT Health Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, and other partners are working together to contain the infection and prevent further spread. Nigeria’s health minister Ali Pate. While urging public and private health facilities to remain on high alert, stressing that health workers must maintain a high index of suspicion for possible cases, he called on Nigerians to remain calm and vigilant. The minister advised the public to practise good hygiene, watch out for symptoms including fever, weakness, headache and diarrhoea, and cooperate with public health officials. He maintained that the situation is being managed, with the government pledging timely and transparent updates as efforts continue to contain the virus. The health minister said the government is drawing on Nigeria’s experience in containing the 2014 Ebola outbreak and the public health mechanisms established over the years, adding that all identified contacts are being traced and monitored. A health worker prepares to administer a vaccine developed for a strain of the Ebola virus at the Provincial Laboratory of Ituri in the northeastern province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, on September 19, 2026. Reacting to the report, however, in a public statement issued on Tuesday, the Ugandan ministry said “The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said, adding that travel through Uganda alone was insufficient to establish where the infection occurred. It also said the Nigerian government had yet to provide detailed information about the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history, which it said would help guide further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. The Ugandan health ministry said it was working with relevant agencies to strengthen screening and public health controls at points of entry, following the development. It added that limited provisions had been maintained for humanitarian and diplomatic movements. Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate using a manikin the evacuation protocols of deceased victims of Ebola during a training by a medical charity in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) at Ongata Rongai, Kajiado County in Kenya on July 10, 2026. Kenya, which confirmed its first imported case in early October, reported a ninth case on Tuesday. Its health ministry said all nine cases belonged to one known cluster, with the eight surviving patients responding well to supportive care. The first Kenyan patient had travelled from the DRC through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi. The development has heightened regional concerns about the movement of the virus across borders. Uganda also recorded Ebola infections earlier in 2026 but subsequently declared its outbreak over after completing the required period without a new confirmed case. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or with contaminated materials. Symptoms can include fever, headache, severe weakness, vomiting and diarrhoea. The post Uganda Debunks Claims Of Ebola Outbreak After Nigeria Confirmed Infection appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Happiness is the next AI KPI if Oxford boffins have their way
item.description: Mass unemployment, boiling the planet, and human extinction within a decade: the dystopian visions of AI are well rehearsed. Academics now argue that EU policymakers should ensure the taxpayers helping to fund the tech get something back, a “happiness dividend.” Researchers at the Oxford Internet Institute (OII), led by Professor Sandra Wachter, say citizens who are inadvertently helping to create the next generation of tech billionaires need more than promises that AI will boost economic growth and fatten corporate profits. Their paper, " Optimising for happiness in EU technology policy to repay public subsidies for AI ," published in the Royal Society Open Science, notes that the public backs AI development through funding, tax breaks, and access to land, water, energy, infrastructure, and data. On data, most people have no say in the matter. Creative work, social media posts, and user interactions have all been swept up to train frontier models, spurring a stream of lawsuits . The OII team proposes happiness as a third goal for AI heavyweights, alongside economic growth and risk mitigation. “Making technology less harmful is not the same as making it socially beneficial,” the researchers told us. What makes people happy? The researchers point to relatedness, competence, and autonomy, all of which some uses of AI could undermine. Chatbots that mimic human emotion may erode the value people place on real human connection. Heavy reliance on AI could dull skills . AI influence could make it harder for people to make their own choices . And datacenters threaten land and water, leaving fewer trees and green spaces for people to connect with nature. “Under the proposed approach, companies benefiting from public support would be expected to predict how their technologies will improve happiness and well-being, and be held accountable for delivering those benefits,” the researchers said. The EU has allocated €20 billion for AI gigafactories , while GenAI4EU and the Digital Europe programme is using €700 million through Horizon research projects into generative AI and supercomputing initiatives. “The public already pays for AI through subsidies, resources, and data, yet has little say over what it gets in return,” said lead author Professor Sandra Wachter. “We believe people deserve technology that increases their happiness. If the public is helping to build the AI industry, it should also share in its benefits.” Denser, more powerful servers in a growing number of datacenters are drawing more energy, potentially pushing up household electricity bills . Memory makers are prioritizing higher-margin chips, so ordinary DRAM and NAND cost more, and so do the devices that use them . Water, which some see as the planet’s next most precious commodity, is being used to cool server racks . item.content:encoded: Mass unemployment, boiling the planet, and human extinction within a decade: the dystopian visions of AI are well rehearsed. Academics now argue that EU policymakers should ensure the taxpayers helping to fund the tech get something back, a “happiness dividend.” Researchers at the Oxford Internet Institute (OII), led by Professor Sandra Wachter, say citizens who are inadvertently helping to create the next generation of tech billionaires need more than promises that AI will boost economic growth and fatten corporate profits. Their paper, " Optimising for happiness in EU technology policy to repay public subsidies for AI ," published in the Royal Society Open Science, notes that the public backs AI development through funding, tax breaks, and access to land, water, energy, infrastructure, and data. On data, most people have no say in the matter. Creative work, social media posts, and user interactions have all been swept up to train frontier models, spurring a stream of lawsuits . The OII team proposes happiness as a third goal for AI heavyweights, alongside economic growth and risk mitigation. “Making technology less harmful is not the same as making it socially beneficial,” the researchers told us. What makes people happy? The researchers point to relatedness, competence, and autonomy, all of which some uses of AI could undermine. Chatbots that mimic human emotion may erode the value people place on real human connection. Heavy reliance on AI could dull skills . AI influence could make it harder for people to make their own choices . And datacenters threaten land and water, leaving fewer trees and green spaces for people to connect with nature. “Under the proposed approach, companies benefiting from public support would be expected to predict how their technologies will improve happiness and well-being, and be held accountable for delivering those benefits,” the researchers said. The EU has allocated €20 billion for AI gigafactories , while GenAI4EU and the Digital Europe programme is using €700 million through Horizon research projects into generative AI and supercomputing initiatives. “The public already pays for AI through subsidies, resources, and data, yet has little say over what it gets in return,” said lead author Professor Sandra Wachter. “We believe people deserve technology that increases their happiness. If the public is helping to build the AI industry, it should also share in its benefits.” Denser, more powerful servers in a growing number of datacenters are drawing more energy, potentially pushing up household electricity bills . Memory makers are prioritizing higher-margin chips, so ordinary DRAM and NAND cost more, and so do the devices that use them . Water, which some see as the planet’s next most precious commodity, is being used to cool server racks . Anthropic warned this year that humanity risks courting extinction unless powerful models are properly controlled. Last year it and OpenAI raised the prospect of mass unemployment as employers turn to AI to cut costs. The researchers add that the difficulty of getting data out of model makers and their cloud providers makes it harder to gauge the environmental damage datacenters are doing. Against that backdrop, finding some way to improve people’s well-being looks essential. Will the model makers take note? Even pessimists are sometimes pleasantly surprised, though we expect profits will trump pleasantness. ®

item.title: How to Protect Yourself From Ebola Virus Disease
item.description: PPE Preparation in an Ebola Clinic. Generated Image. Yesterday, October 20, 2026, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) announced the confirmation of the first Ebola virus disease case in Abuja. While the federal government and the NCDC have continued strengthening surveillance and response efforts to prevent its spread, it is important for Nigerian citizens to also stay alert, safe and take preventive measures. According to the NCDC , “Ebola virus disease (EVD), also known as Ebola hemorrhagic fever (EHF), is a severe disease of humans and other primates caused by an RNA virus of the family Filoviridae and genus Ebola virus. The disease has a high fatality rate, killing between 25%-90% of those infected. Research conducted in 2005 suggested fruit bats to be the likely reservoir due to their ability to spread the virus without being affected by it. The largest outbreak to date took place in West Africa between March 2014 and June 2016, affecting Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Nigeria primarily. A total of 11,296 cases were recorded, including suspected and probable cases.” The first-ever case of Ebola in Nigeria was confirmed in Lagos on 23 July 2014, and with its high fatality rate, citizens need to understand how to protect themselves before the government’s intervention. According to the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Affairs , here are how you can protect yourself from Ebola virus disease: Advice to Nigerians Nigerians are advised to: Practice good hand hygiene. Wash your hands regularly with soap under running water or use hand sanitisers when soap and water are not readily available. Avoid physical contact with anyone who has symptoms of an infection with an unknown diagnosis. Reduce the risk of wildlife-to-human transmission from contact with infected fruit bats or monkeys/apes and the consumption of raw meat. Animals should be handled with gloves and other appropriate protective clothing. Animal products should be thoroughly cooked before consumption. Avoid direct contact with the blood, saliva, vomit, urine and other bodily fluids of suspected or confirmed EVD cases. If you or someone you know (with a travel history to any country with Ebola cases) experiences symptoms of EVD enumerated above, call 6232 or your State Ministry of Health hotline IMMEDIATELY for guidance. Advice to Healthcare Workers Healthcare workers: Are advised to maintain a high index of suspicion for EVD in their encounter with their patients Ensure strict isolation of the patient(s). Adhere strictly to infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) like face masks, hand gloves, appropriate gowns, safe sharps disposal and others. Report suspected cases immediately to the NCDC or State Ministry of Health for appropriate response and management. Advice to Travellers Travellers are advised to: Shelter-in-place to avoid further spread through shared transport

item.content:encoded: PPE Preparation in an Ebola Clinic. Generated Image. Yesterday, October 20, 2026, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) announced the confirmation of the first Ebola virus disease case in Abuja. While the federal government and the NCDC have continued strengthening surveillance and response efforts to prevent its spread, it is important for Nigerian citizens to also stay alert, safe and take preventive measures. According to the NCDC , “Ebola virus disease (EVD), also known as Ebola hemorrhagic fever (EHF), is a severe disease of humans and other primates caused by an RNA virus of the family Filoviridae and genus Ebola virus. The disease has a high fatality rate, killing between 25%-90% of those infected. Research conducted in 2005 suggested fruit bats to be the likely reservoir due to their ability to spread the virus without being affected by it. The largest outbreak to date took place in West Africa between March 2014 and June 2016, affecting Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Nigeria primarily. A total of 11,296 cases were recorded, including suspected and probable cases.” The first-ever case of Ebola in Nigeria was confirmed in Lagos on 23 July 2014, and with its high fatality rate, citizens need to understand how to protect themselves before the government’s intervention. According to the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Affairs , here are how you can protect yourself from Ebola virus disease: Advice to Nigerians Nigerians are advised to: Practice good hand hygiene. Wash your hands regularly with soap under running water or use hand sanitisers when soap and water are not readily available. Avoid physical contact with anyone who has symptoms of an infection with an unknown diagnosis. Reduce the risk of wildlife-to-human transmission from contact with infected fruit bats or monkeys/apes and the consumption of raw meat. Animals should be handled with gloves and other appropriate protective clothing. Animal products should be thoroughly cooked before consumption. Avoid direct contact with the blood, saliva, vomit, urine and other bodily fluids of suspected or confirmed EVD cases. If you or someone you know (with a travel history to any country with Ebola cases) experiences symptoms of EVD enumerated above, call 6232 or your State Ministry of Health hotline IMMEDIATELY for guidance. Advice to Healthcare Workers Healthcare workers: Are advised to maintain a high index of suspicion for EVD in their encounter with their patients Ensure strict isolation of the patient(s). Adhere strictly to infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) like face masks, hand gloves, appropriate gowns, safe sharps disposal and others. Report suspected cases immediately to the NCDC or State Ministry of Health for appropriate response and management. Advice to Travellers Travellers are advised to: Shelter-in-place to avoid further spread through shared transport systems (public or private) until health authorities reach out. Await dedicated responders for assessment and possible transport to a designated treatment centre if required. Ebola symptoms can vary, but the most commonly experienced symptoms at the beginning of the disease include a sudden onset of fever, intense weakness, muscle pain, headache, and a sore throat. As the disease progresses, other symptoms may develop, such as vomiting, diarrhea and jaundice (yellowness of the eyes). In severe cases, individuals may experience uncontrolled bleeding from body orifices and dysfunction or failure of several organs, including the kidneys, liver, and central nervous system. This can lead to shock and, ultimately, death. In fatal cases, death often occurs between 8 and 9 days after the onset of symptoms. Please contact NCDC for more enquiries or to report a suspected case on the toll-free number: 6232. Stay safe, Nigerians. item.title: 17 Years Later, Johnny Depp’s Overlooked Action Crime Thriller Is Officially Free on YouTube
item.description: Based on Bryan Burrough’s nonfiction book of the same name, Michael Mann’s Public Enemies puts Depp in the shoes of John Dillinger, one of the most prolific bank robbers in American history, set during his final few months of thieving in 1934. As he wreaks havoc across the Midwest, Dillenger attempts to stay one step ahead of Melvin Purvis (Christian Bale), a ruthless federal agent tasked with finally bringing him justice. With a proven track record of bringing crime epics to life, from Miami Vice to Heat , Mann captures a transformative moment when the relationship between criminals, the public, and the authorities was rapidly shifting. Dillinger became a symbol of defiance during the Great Depression, when banks were the furthest thing from beloved institutions, while the newly empowered FBI was working to establish itself as a formidable national force. The film’s historical scope is narrower than Burrough’s sprawling account of America’s crime wave, but that focus gives Mann room to explore the mythology surrounding one particularly charismatic outlaw.

item.title: The Opposition Has A Numbers Problem. Tinubu Has A Trust Problem
item.description: Nigeria’s presidential election is less than three months away, and something rather curious is happening. The ruling party is gathering supporters from almost every political direction. The opposition is gathering presidential candidates who cannot quite agree on who should lead them. And the electorate is being asked to choose between an administration defending difficult economic reforms and challengers promising a different future. There is plenty of political activity. What remains less clear is whether there is enough political persuasion. This Tuesday, three developments help explain where the race is heading: growing divisions within the opposition, a new controversy over the security of a presidential candidate, and an increasingly uncomfortable argument about who should bear the cost of Nigeria’s economic reforms. Together, they point to a contest that may ultimately be decided not by the size of political rallies, but by the credibility of the choices placed before Nigerians. 1. The opposition’s arithmetic is becoming complicated. (L-R) Kwankwaso and Atiku For months, the argument for a united opposition has seemed straightforward. If President Bola Tinubu’s opponents could combine their electoral strengths, they might present a formidable challenge to the APC. The difficulty, of course, is deciding whose name should appear at the top of the ticket. The latest reports suggest that this problem is becoming more pronounced. A coalition initiative involving several opposition parties is exploring the possibility of a common presidential candidate. But supporters of Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi are already disagreeing over who should lead such an arrangement. Rabiu Kwankwaso’s camp has also rejected suggestions that he should step aside for Atiku, while other presidential contenders continue to defend their ambitions. This is no longer merely a disagreement about personalities. It is a disagreement about the nature of the opposition itself. Should the objective be to assemble the largest possible coalition around the most experienced political operator? Or should it be to offer Nigerians a genuinely different political direction? Atiku’s supporters can argue that he has national networks, experience and an established electoral base. Obi’s supporters can point to his appeal among voters seeking a break from traditional politics. Kwankwaso’s political organisation offers another constituency that cannot simply be wished away. But there is an uncomfortable truth for all three camps. Votes are not bags of rice that politicians can simply transfer from one warehouse to another. A coalition agreement signed in Abuja does not guarantee that voters in Kano, Onitsha, Ibadan or Port Harcourt will follow the instructions of their preferred politicians. And the longer these negotiations continue, the less time remains for building the trust, campaign organisation and common policy programme needed to make a joint ticket credible.
