item.title: Emir of Kano to Lead Sustainability Leaders at STS’ 10-Year Milestone in Lagos
item.description: With four years remaining to the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals deadline, the Sustainability Table Discourse Series (STS) will mark its tenth anniversary on 15–16 October 2026 at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos, with a deliberate shift from dialogue to delivery. Under the theme ‘Leading the Sustainable Development Agenda: People, Planet and Prosperity,’ STS @10 will bring together leaders from government, business, finance, development institutions, technology and civil society to address a defining question: how can Africa bridge the gap between sustainable development ambition and execution? Headlining the gathering is H.H. Muhammadu Sanusi II , Emir of Kano , who will deliver the Flagship Keynote, “People, Planet & Prosperity: The Decade of Delivery.” The gathering will also feature H.E. Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, Deputy Governor of Lagos State; Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State and Chairman, Forum of State Commissioners of Finance; H.E. Amb. Prof. (Mrs.) Olufolake AbdulRazaq, First Lady of Kwara State; Tenioye Majekodunmi, Director-General, National Council on Climate Change; Dr. Innocent Barikor, Director-General/CEO, NESREA; Rukaiya El-Rufai, Presidency / National Economic Council & Climate Change; Adam Boros, Vice President, Africa Finance Corporation; Ademola Ogunbanjo, President & CEO, Oando Clean Energy; Rolake Akinkugbe-Filani, CEO, EnergyInc Advisors Limited; and Dapo Otunla, Chief Corporate Services Officer, IHS Nigeria, among other leaders. The current programme also features a high-level dialogue on mobilizing capital and leadership for Africa’s sustainability transition. First convened in 2016, STS has spent a decade bringing together stakeholders around the green economy, climate finance, technology, circularity, food security, ESG and the Sustainable Development Goals. STS @10 marks an inflection point: a greater focus on bridging Africa’s sustainability implementation gap—the distance between commitments and action, innovation and scale, and viable projects and the investment required to deliver them. “Africa does not suffer from a shortage of ambition, declarations or conferences. The real deficit is execution—turning policy into implementation, innovation into scale and credible projects into investible opportunities,” said Kayode Olaniyan , Convener of the Sustainability Table Discourse Series. “Ten years of STS have shown us the power of bringing the right people to the table. But the next decade must be about what happens after they leave it. We are not convening another talk shop. The next decade must be aboutdelivery,” He added. The programme will focus on four critical conversations: Nigeria’s energy future and expanding energy access; Technology, AI and the SDGs; the circular economy and responsible production; and resilient food systems, smarter value chains and cold-chain infrastructure. The current programme also features a high-level dialogue on mobilizing capital and leadership for Africa’s sustainability transition. First convened in 2016, STS has spent a decade bringing together stakeholders around the green economy, climate finance, technology, circularity, food security, ESG and the Sustainable Development Goals. But the next decade must be about what happens after they leave it. We are not convening another talk shop. The next decade must be aboutdelivery,” He added. The programme will focus on four critical conversations: Nigeria’s energy future and expanding energy access; Technology, AI and the SDGs; the circular economy and responsible production; and resilient food systems, smarter value chains and cold-chain infrastructure. Beyond the conversations, STS @10 will move from ideas to investment and innovation. Day Two will feature masterclasses, strategic investment engagements, the STS @10 Investment & Deals Room — Connecting Capital with Projects and Enterprise, and an Innovation Pitch Finale & Investor Showcase, creating opportunities to connect promising businesses and projects with financial institutions, investors and development partners. A New Era of Action. The gala programme confirms both the book launch and documentary premiere as part of the anniversary celebrations. Ten years ago, STS created a table for the conversation. At STS @10, the question is no longer simply who is at the table—but what gets done because they were there. item.title: From Asake’s Oba to Omah Lay’s Canada Breeze: 5 Music Videos to Watch
item.description: On set for his Oba music video, Asake highlights his signature high-steeze look with a textured jacket and luxury travel accessories. Music is a daily business in Nigeria, both for the artists making it and the listeners who keep up with new releases. Almost every week, new songs drop alongside music videos that bring them to life visually. This week, we’re putting you on five new music videos to check out, featuring Asake , Omah Lay , FOLA , and Young Jonn . Here are five new Nigerian music videos that are worth adding to your watch list this week: Asake – Oba Asake takes fans into the creative process behind “Oba,” trading elaborate street scenes for a more intimate look at a late-night recording session. Directed by Director Buise, the video features the singer alongside producers and backing vocalists, while his signature style and confident presence reinforce the royal theme of the song. The track appears on his M$NEY album. Omah Lay – Canada Breeze Omah Lay’s “Canada Breeze” captures the singer’s reflective side, touching on personal growth, spirituality and finding peace after periods of worry. The song, from his Clarity of Mind album, pairs his signature melodic delivery with lyrics about moving beyond past struggles. Its music video gives fans another way to experience the record’s introspective mood. FOLA – miss you ii FOLA returns to matters of the heart with “miss you ii (nriri),” a release that speaks to longing and missing someone. The track features the Nigerian singer’s melodic Afropop style and arrives as part of a busy period for the rising artist, whose 9 album was released in October 2026. Fans can check out the song’s lyric video and follow its story through the lyrics. Omah Lay – Artificial Happiness Omah Lay takes a cinematic approach to “Artificial Happiness,” the opening track of his Clarity of Mind album. In the video, the singer awakens in an abandoned warehouse with a white tree at its centre, surrounded by mysterious figures whose movements give the scene an unsettling quality. Co-directed creatively by Omah Lay and his longtime collaborator NWSPK, the visual explores the song’s introspective world and the search for genuine happiness. Young Jonn – Glass in the Air Young Jonn brings dancefloor energy to “Glass in the Air.” The song reflects the excitement of navigating new territory and celebrating personal milestones, with the producer-turned-singer leaning into an upbeat, dance-ready sound. It is another opportunity to experience the infectious energy and melodic style that have become central to his evolution as an artist. The post From Asake’s Oba to Omah Lay’s Canada Breeze: 5 Music Videos to Watch appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: 5 Films Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson Have Featured in Together
item.description: Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson in western bridal styling for “My 30th Wedding”. If it were rumoured that Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson are getting married, you’d hardly dismiss the rumour because of the times the duo have shared the stage in films, and their synergy and connection each time they appear together in a film. With their latest YouTube release , “My 30th Wedding” going viral, with over 22 million views in 11 days, it is informative to look at some of the films they have both featured in together. In each film, you will find that connection. While they have mainly featured together in romance movies, the genre has not limited the creativity and energy they bring into each film. Let’s look at some of the films Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson have both featured in. Breaded Life In this 2021 movie, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson navigate life in the ghetto after Timini’s character, Sunmi, is forced out of his wealthy existence. The film showcases the duo’s varying personas, highlighting themes of vulnerability, strength, and love. They demonstrate how two actors can continuously interact on screen while still delivering distinctly different vibes. Reel Love Produced by Timini Egbuson and directed by Kayode Kasum, Reel Love explores the relationship between love, celebrity and social media. Timini plays Tomide Jobi, a relationship influencer whose public image suffers after a heated confrontation with Rachel, played by T.J. Omusuku, goes viral. To repair the damage, Tomide agrees to stage a fake relationship with Rachel, but the arrangement becomes complicated when genuine feelings begin to develop. Bimbo Ademoye appears as Chizaram in the film, which also features Funke Akindele, Shaffy Bello and Dakore Egbuson-Akande. Released in Nigerian cinemas on Valentine’s Day in 2025, the film examines the pressure to maintain a public image and the difference between performing love for an audience and experiencing it in real life. Big Love In Big Love, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson play Adina and Adil, two young people who meet while pursuing their ambitions and eventually fall in love. Adil is determined to achieve his dreams, while Adina is an independent woman focused on making a living. As their relationship develops, they must confront personal fears and a secret that threatens to come between them. Directed by Biodun Stephen, the romantic drama explores love, trust and the difficult choices that can test a relationship. The film also gives viewers another opportunity to see the chemistry between the two actors as romantic leads. Unexpected Places Bimbo Ademoye plays Prosper, the daughter of a housekeeper who steps in to manage the household while her mother recovers from surgery. Her new responsibilities bring her into contact with Chris, played by Timini Egbuson, a wealthy playboy whose irresponsible behaviour has become a concern for his father. item.title: Midea Launches WIN 9JA WIN Promotion with Guaranteed Rewards and Chery Tiggo 2 Pro Grand Prize
item.description: Midea has announced the launch of WIN 9JA WIN , a nationwide consumer promotion designed to reward Nigerians who choose Midea home appliances during the 2026 festive shopping season. Running from 10 October to 31 December 2026 , the promotion gives every qualifying shopper an instant opportunity to win, with a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro positioned as the ultimate grand prize. Under the promotion, consumers who purchase any Midea product worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer receive a scratch voucher at the point of purchase. The shopper scratches the voucher to reveal the reward won, creating a simple and immediate link between purchase and reward. Every qualifying shopper is a winner, subject to the approved campaign terms and conditions. The campaign combines retail participation with radio, digital, public relations, in-store visibility and an extensive on-ground Promo Tour Truck programme. The touring activation will carry the excitement of WIN 9JA WIN into selected markets and dealer locations, with the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro prominently showcased to give consumers a close view of the campaign’s headline prize. A Consumer Promotion Built Around Instant Reward WIN 9JA WIN is designed to make the festive purchase journey more rewarding while strengthening engagement between Midea , its dealer network and consumers across Nigeria. Its central proposition is straightforward: make a qualifying purchase, receive a scratch voucher and discover the reward immediately. The approved reward pool spans Midea home appliances and branded consumer gifts. These include side-by-side refrigerators, chest freezers, air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, air fryers, microwave ovens, kettles, standing fans and blenders, as well as branded T-shirts, caps and pens. The ultimate reward is a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro, presented in the campaign materials as the car to be won. MIDEA NIGERIA | MEDIA RELEASE How Consumers Can Participate Step Consumer action Purchase Buy any Midea product or combination of eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer between 10 October and 31 December 2026. Receive Collect the campaign scratch voucher issued for the qualifying purchase. Scratch Scratch the voucher to reveal the reward. Claim Follow the verification and prize-claim guidance provided by the participating dealer in accordance with the approved campaign terms and conditions. Additional Midea Air Conditioner Offer Alongside WIN 9JA WIN, Midea is also offering free installation and a free copper kit to consumers who purchase any Midea air conditioner from 1 October through 31 December 2026. The offer extends the campaign’s value beyond the product purchase by helping eligible AC buyers with installation support, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Promo Tour Truck Takes WIN 9JA WIN Closer to Consumers A major feature of the campaign is the branded Promo Tour Truck programme, developed as a mobile visibility and engagement platform.

The offer extends the campaign’s value beyond the product purchase by helping eligible AC buyers with installation support, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Promo Tour Truck Takes WIN 9JA WIN Closer to Consumers A major feature of the campaign is the branded Promo Tour Truck programme, developed as a mobile visibility and engagement platform. The vehicle format is designed to operate as a moving billboard and activation hub, carrying Midea branding, product communication and WIN 9JA WIN messaging through high-traffic retail corridors and participating dealer locations. The Chery Tiggo 2 Pro will be prominently showcased as part of the tour, allowing shoppers and local communities to see the campaign’s ultimate prize at close range. At scheduled dealer stops, consumers will be able to discover Midea products, receive clear information about the promotion and understand the qualifying purchase and scratch-voucher process. The programme is intended to support participating dealers, stimulate retail interest and bring the promotion into the communities where consumers shop. Selected Tour Markets and Dealer Locations The supplied tour schedule covers selected locations across Lagos, the South-West, South-South, South- East, North-Central and Northern Nigeria. The dealer activation routes are scheduled from 10 October to 1 November 2026, subject to final operational confirmation. The market clusters are listed below; the detailed dealer-location appendix forms part of this release pack. East Route : Port Harcourt, Aba, Umuahia, Uyo and Oron, Owerri, Nnewi, Onitsha, Awka, Asaba and Enugu. Lagos and adjoining markets : Lekki, Victoria Island, Ikoyi, Ajah, Lagos Island, Idumota, Apapa, Festac, Alaba, Ojo, Ikotun, Igando, Idimu, Ipaja, Abule Egba, Agege, Ikeja, Allen, Maryland, Ogba, Yaba, Surulere, Ebute Metta, Ikorodu, Badagry, Ota, Agbara and Isheri. South-West and South-South route: Ibadan, Iseyin, Ogbomoso, Ilorin, Osogbo, Ilesa, Ile-Ife, Abeokuta, Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye, Mowe, Warri, Effurun, Ughelli, Sapele, Benin City, Irrua, Uromi, Akure and Ondo. North and North-Central Route: Abuja, Mararaba, Lokoja, Makurdi, Lafia, Kaduna, Kano, Yola and Jimeta. Supporting Retail Engagement and Household Choice The campaign reflects Midea’s focus on making home-appliance technology more accessible and relevant to Nigerian households. By combining guaranteed rewards with a wide dealer footprint and direct market engagement, WIN 9JA WIN gives consumers another reason to explore Midea’s range of air conditioners, refrigerators, freezers, washing machines, cooking appliances and small domestic appliances during the year-end season. Executive Comment / Quotation “WIN 9JA WIN is our way of thanking Nigerian consumers and making every qualifying purchase more rewarding. The mechanic is simple, transparent and immediate: buy, receive a scratch voucher and reveal your reward. Through the Promo Tour Truck programme, we are also taking the campaign closer to our dealer partners and consumers in markets across the country, while giving shoppers the opportunity to experience Midea products and see the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro grand prize up close.” – Ashok Dimri, Business Head, Africa, of Care Global Consumer Ltd. Call to Action Consumers can visit participating Midea dealers nationwide between 10 October and 31 December 2026, purchase eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more and collect a scratch voucher to reveal their reward. Consumers purchasing any Midea air conditioner can also access the free installation and free copper kit offer through 31 December 2026, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. About Midea Group Midea is one of over 10 brands operating under the Smart Home Business of Midea Group. Midea Group , with the vision of “bringing great innovations to life”, is an international tech-leading company which specializes in seven major business areas: Smart Home, Industrial Technologies, Building Technologies, KUKA, New Energy, Midea Healthcare and ANNTO Logistics. Midea’s products and services have served more than 500 million customers worldwide, including key clients and strategic partners across various industries. Midea operates more than 400 subsidiaries, 41 R&D centres and 65 major manufacturing bases globally, with a business network covering over 200 countries and regions. item.title: Apple AirPods 5 review: the best open-fit earbuds yet
item.description: Upgraded, cheaper AirPods have noise cancelling, sound and controls to rival many plugged-in buds but without tips Apple’s latest AirPods set a new standard for open-fit buds with upgraded noise cancelling that now rivals many plugged-in designs of the same price. The AirPods 5 have the same design the popular AirPods 4 offering an option for those that do not like silicone ear tips used by most noise cancelling earbuds. item.title: Systolic style: meet the medical-grade smartwatch revolutionising blood pressure monitoring
item.description: An estimated one-third of adults in England have high blood pressure, with research showing that many are unaware of their condition. But thanks to the new Huawei Watch D3, monitoring blood pressure is easier, accurate and more stylish than ever Wearable technology has come a long way in the past decade. Take a look around at your colleagues, friends and family, and you’ll be hard pushed to find anyone not wearing some kind of health monitoring ring, watch or band – there are even tracking insoles and patches, too. These gadgets have myriad benefits – not least, allowing us more control and insight over our health and wellbeing than ever before. We’re able to monitor everything from sleep and stress to heart health and more, and the technology is becoming more refined and intuitive seemingly by the day. Continue reading...

item.title: Welcome home, Sophie Adenot
item.description: Video: 00:02:54 After 237 days and over 3,700 orbits around Earth aboard the International Space Station, Sophie Adenot is back on Earth! Following a handover to Crew-13, Sophie and her Crew-12 crewmates undocked on 7 October and splashed down off the coast of California the next day. Now back in Europe, Sophie will begin her post-flight data collection and rehabilitation while readjusting to life on Earth after the longest mission in space by a European astronaut so far. Welcome home, Sophie!

Bringing together media, business partners, retailers, distributors, industry stakeholders and content creators from across the region, the event provided a closer look at TCL’s 2026 display innovations alongside new solutions across air conditioning, refrigeration, laundry and monitors. The launch reflects TCL’s continued investment in Nigeria and its focus on introducing technologies that respond to the way consumers across both markets live today. From larger screens for sport and family entertainment to energy conscious cooling, high capacity appliances and connected home experiences, the new portfolio has been developed to combine performance, convenience and accessibility. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: TCL , a global leader in consumer electronics and No.1 Mini LED and Ultra Large Screen TV Brand (75”+)¹, has showcased its latest consumer electronics and home appliance portfolio for Nigeria during its West Africa regional launch event in Côte d’Ivoire. Bringing together media, business partners, retailers, distributors, industry stakeholders and content creators from across the region, the event provided a closer look at TCL’s 2026 display innovations alongside new solutions across air conditioning, refrigeration, laundry and monitors. From larger screens for sport and family entertainment to energy conscious cooling, high capacity appliances and connected home experiences, the new portfolio has been developed to combine performance, convenience and accessibility. Daniel Ray , Director of Sales, TCL West Africa, said: “ Nigeria are important markets within TCL’s West Africa growth strategy, with consumers increasingly looking for technology that delivers strong performance while remaining relevant to their everyday needs. Through this regional launch, we are bringing together entertainment, cooling and home appliance innovations designed around how people live, connect and enjoy content across both markets. Our ambition is to continue making advanced technology more accessible while giving consumers greater choice across the home. “ A New Era of Premium Big Screen Entertainment Large screen entertainment continues to grow across Nigeria, with consumers increasingly seeking more immersive experiences across sport, movies, streaming and gaming. Leading TCL’s latest television portfolio is the C7L SQD Mini LED range, available from 65 to 98 inches, bringing enhanced colour precision, brightness control, deeper blacks and improved halo control. Complementing the C7L is the 98 inch C6K QD Mini LED TV, delivering an ultra large screen experience with advanced Mini LED performance for movies, live sport and gaming. TCL Brings Premium Large Screen Entertainment to Nigeria with the C7L SQD Mini LED TV The TCL C7L brings the latest generation of SQD Mini LED technology to consumers across Nigeria, with screen sizes ranging from 65 to 98 inches. Designed for immersive home entertainment, it combines advanced Mini LED light control, enhanced colour precision and strong contrast performance across sport, movies, streaming and gaming. The 98 inch model features up to 2,176 Precise Dimming Zones, up to HDR 3,000 nits brightness, up to 100% BT.2020 All Scenes Wide Color Gamut, an HVA 2.0 Pro Panel, Audio by Bang & Olufsen and a 288Hz VRR Game Accelerator. TCL C6K QD Mini LED TV Expands the Ultra Large Screen Experience TCL C6K QD Mini LED TV complements an immersive ultra large screen experience with screen sizes ranging from 65 to 98 inches, combining QD-Mini LED backlighting with quantum dot colour technology for enhanced brightness, contrast and colour performance. It features TCL All Domain Halo Control Technology, up to 512 Precise Dimming Zones, a 144Hz native refresh rate, an AiPQ Pro Processor, a Matte HVA Panel and an ONKYO 2.1 Hi Fi audio system. Smarter Cooling Designed for Local Climate Needs With warm temperatures forming part of everyday life across Nigeria, cooling performance, energy management and convenience remain important considerations for households. TCL highlighted two air conditioning solutions designed to address these priorities, the FreshIN 3.0 and SaveIN AI Series 24K. TCL FreshIN 3.0 FreshIN 3.0 expands the air conditioning experience beyond temperature control by introducing fresh outdoor air into the room while supporting improved indoor air quality. Key technologies include FreshIN Technology, T AI Energy Saving, Smart Voice Control, QuadruPuri filtration, Visible Air Quality and Gentle Breeze. The system is also engineered for stable operation in high ambient temperatures, making it especially relevant for consumers across Nigeria seeking reliable cooling performance during hotter periods of the year. TCL SaveIN AI Series The TCL SaveIN AI Series is designed around efficient everyday cooling, combining T AI Energy Saving, smart Wi Fi control and Coanda Airflow. Its intelligent energy management technology dynamically adjusts compressor performance based on temperature conditions, helping consumers manage cooling more efficiently while maintaining indoor comfort. For households conscious of both comfort and electricity consumption, the SaveIN AI Series offers a smarter approach to everyday cooling through intelligent controls and flexible energy management. Refrigeration Designed for Local Households For many households across Nigeria, refrigeration needs extend beyond everyday food storage to larger family shopping, meal preparation and the need to keep food fresh for longer. TCL’s latest refrigeration range addresses these priorities through generous capacity, flexible storage and reliable cooling, led by the P7 Side by Side Refrigerator and C7 Cross Door Refrigerator. TCL P7 Side by Side Refrigerator The TCL P774SBBG is a large capacity side by side refrigerator designed for households that require generous storage space for fresh and frozen food. Featuring a premium black glass finish, the model combines No Frost cooling, inverter technology, electronic controls and multi airflow functionality to support consistent cooling and convenient food organisation. Its larger format makes it particularly suited to family households looking for greater storage flexibility without compromising on contemporary kitchen design. TCL C7 Cross Door Refrigerator The TCL C780CDN introduces a spacious four door format that allows households to organise groceries, frozen food and everyday essentials more easily. Combining No Frost cooling with inverter performance, the model has been designed around flexibility, capacity and convenience, responding to the needs of households looking for practical food storage alongside a premium kitchen aesthetic. Smarter Laundry for Busy Households with the TCL C5 Washer Dryer The TCL C5 washer dryer combines a 12 kg washing capacity with TCL Super Drum technology, providing additional washing space and improved fabric movement. Its feature set includes Auto Dose, jetBubble technology, Wi Fi connectivity, Steam Wash, activeFresh, Dynamic Rinse and quick wash programmes. The large capacity format is particularly suited to family households, while its connected features and automatic washing functions help reduce the effort required for everyday laundry and fabric care. Strengthening TCL’s Presence Across Nigeria The regional launch underlines TCL’s strategy to strengthen its presence across Nigeria through a broader product ecosystem and closer collaboration with local distributors, retailers, media and technology communities. By combining global product innovation with a stronger understanding of local consumer priorities, TCL aims to deliver products that are relevant across different areas of everyday life, from entertainment and cooling to food storage, laundry and connected displays. Daniel Ray added: “Our focus is to strengthen TCL’s presence market by market, with products that respond to the needs of the consumers we serve. In Nigeria, that means bringing together larger and more immersive entertainment, efficient cooling, greater household capacity and smarter connected experiences. We see significant potential across both markets and will continue working closely with our partners to make TCL technology more widely available.” Availability Product sizes, specifications, pricing and availability may vary by market. For further information, please visit SIMS Nigeria https://simsng.com/tcl-store/ . About TCL TCL is a leading consumer electronics brand and leader in the global television industry.

item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac mini M6 review: truly mighty but now more pricey
item.description: Apple’s cheapest desktop computer is no longer a bargain but its newest, fastest chip makes it a pocket powerhouse Apple’s latest Mac mini brings real speed and power for far more than everyday tasks in a practically pocketable form you can fit almost anywhere. The impressive new desktop machine is the first to receive an update to Apple’s latest M6 chip while remaining smaller than a headphones box. It is the cheapest computer Apple sells with an M-series chip, but like every other memory-containing piece of electronics, it has been hit by RAMageddon , driving up the starting price to £899 (€1,049/$899/A$1,449) from the £599 or equivalent of its M4 predecessor. Continue reading...

item.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
item.description: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.

item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift
item.description: Technicians prepare to transfer the #2 RS-25 SLS (Space Launch System) rocket engine (front) to the work stand with the #3 engine (back) for integration with the Artemis III core stage rocket on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. During Artemis III, the four RS‑25 engines will launch the Orion spacecraft and its crew of four into low Earth orbit, generating more than two million pounds of thrust at liftoff.

item.title: Microsoft Surface Laptop 8 review: a quality PC whose trackpad taps you back
item.description: Snappy performance, long battery life, great keyboard and excellent new haptic touchpad make the best of Windows 11 Microsoft’s Surface laptop for consumers is back, faster and with longer battery life and a hefty price increase because of the high cost of memory and chips. The Surface Laptop 8 is a straight replacement for the seventh edition from 2024, which was the first of Microsoft’s new generation of ARM-based, Qualcomm-powered PCs designed to better rival Apple’s MacBook Air and other thin and light machines. Continue reading...

item.title: Intuitive living is the latest wellness trend – meet the new tech making it work
item.description: Wellness culture can be overwhelming, but a more fluid approach is emerging. Smart devices such as the Huawei Watch Fit 5 perfectly embody this shift in direction – whether you’re regularly sleep tracking or just occasionally using data to support your lifestyle When it comes to the world of health and wellness, it’s easy to suffer from information overwhelm. We’ve never had more access to data, research and expertise which, while valuable, isn’t always applicable to our own lives. What’s more, few of us have time to spend hours sifting through content to devise a personalised health routine, let alone work out if a “routine” is necessary at all. All this information and expectation can come at a cost: emotional strain, guilt and confusion about where to turn. Health and fitness then start to feel like abstract milestones that we’re blindly chasing rather than important components of our lives. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of ‘earvolution’: from ceremonial piercings to fashion-statement earbuds
item.description: For millennia, humans have been captivated by ear decorations. Now, earbuds not only connect us to the digital world, they also showcase our personal sense of style – and the HUAWEI FreeClip 2 is at the forefront of that development When we are born, a cry can let the world know that we are healthy and OK. When we first begin to talk, we learn to express our needs and understand the needs of others. As we grow older, we learn that the sound of a siren denotes danger, that certain notes swelling together create the sound of a favourite song which lifts our spirits, or that a warm familiar voice on the other end of the phone means our best friend has our back. Our ears give us grounding and clues: they are our maps of the world, guiding us towards truth, keeping us from harm, giving us a constant stream of sensory information. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more.
